In both the bright half of the month and the dark half of the month, Nanda, Bhadra, Jaya, Rikta and Poorna (in three frequencies) are respectively the names of the tithis. The three frequencies of the bright half of the month are respectively inauspicious, medium in auspiciousness and fully auspicious and; the three frequencies of the dark half of the month are regarded respectively fully auspicious, medium in auspiciousness and inauspicious. If, in both the bright and the dark half of the month, the tithis Nanda etc. in order (of all the three frequencies) happen to fall on Friday, Wednesday, Tuesday, Saturday and Thursday, then on that day there is the Siddha Yoga.

AMRITA YOGA AND DAGDHA YOGA ON DAYS SUN- DAY ETC. If on days Sunday, Monday and so on there happen to fall respectively Nanda, Bhadra, Nanda, Jaya, Rikta, Bhadra and Poorna, then there is Amrita Yoga. In the same way, if there happens to fall the Nakshtra of Bharani on Sunday, Chitra on Monday, Uttara shadha on Tuesday, Dhanishtha on Wednesday, Uttara phalguni on Thursday, Jyeshtha on Friday and Rewati on Saturday, Daghda Yoga happens to be on that day

KARKACHA AND SAMVARTAKA YOGA: If Shashthi etc tithis in right order of tithis fall on Saturday etc in reverse order of days, there is Adhama Yoga (Krakacha) on these days. There is Adhama (Samvartaka) yoga also if Pratipada (1) falls on Wednesday and Saptami (7) falls on Sunday. And teeth should not be cleaned with Neem stick etc on the Shashthi (6) etc. Tithis.

On Shashthi (6), Ashtmi (8), Chaturdashi (14), Amavasya (30) tithis are prohibited respectively for oiling (the hair), eating flesh, shaving and sexual intercourse with one’s wife. Ubatan (paste made of turmeric etc used to cleanse the body) should not be applied on the body on Trayodashi (13), Dashmi (10) and Dwitiya (2) and bath should not be taken after rubbing Amla (a fruit) on the body on Amavasya (30), Saptami (7) and Navami (9).

That is, if the Shashthi tithi (6) falls on Saturday oil may be applied on the body, flesh may be eaten on the Durgashtami (8) of the month of Ashwina (coincident with October), shaving may be done on Chaturdashi at a place of pilgrimage and sexual intercourse may be indulged in on the Amavasya of Deepawali (one of the four chief festivals of the Hindus falling on the 30th tithi of the Hindi month of Kartika) One more fact is to be kept in mind here that the tithi which remains on that day for two or three hours after Sunrise is not the one on which the above said things should not be done. Thus, suppose the Shashthi tithi (6) remains (on Saturday) only for 2 hours after the Sunrise, then oil may be applied on the body 2 hours after Sunrise.

DAGDHA, VISHA, HUTASHANA AND YAMAGHANTA YOGAS. If Dwadashi tithi (12) happens to fall on Sunday, Ekadashi (11) on Monday, Panchami (5) on Tuesday, Tritiya (3) on Wednesday, Shashthi (6) on Thursday, Ashtami (8) on Friday and Navami (9) on Saturday, the yoga formed on these days is Dagdha. Again, if Chaturthi tithi (4) happens to fall on Sunday, Shashthi (6) on Monday, Saptami (7) on Tuesday, Dwitiya (2) on Wednesday, Ashtami (8) on Thursday, Navami (9) on Friday and Saptami (7) on Saturday, the yoga formed on these days is called 'Visha'. In the same way, if the Dwadashi tithi (12) happens to fall on Sunday, Shashthi (6) on Monday, Saptami (7) on Tuesday, Ashtami (8) on Wednesday, Navami (9) on Thursday, Dashmi (10) on Friday and Ekadashi (11) on Saturday, the yoga formed on these days is called 'Hutashana' yoga. Similarly, if the Makha Nakshtra happens to be there on Sunday, Vishakha on Monday, Aridra on Tuesday, Moola on Wednesday, Kritika on Thursday, Rohini on Friday and Hasta on Saturday, the yoga formed on these days in these Nakshtras is Yama Ghanta

ZERO TITHIS OF CHAITRADI MASAS or MONTHS IN BOTH THE PAKSHAS (The bright and the dark half of the month):- Pratipada and Dwitiya (1 and 2) tithis in the month of Bhadrapada (August). Dwitiya and Tritiya (2 and 3) in Shravana (August). Dwadashi (12) in Baisakha (April). Chaturthi and Panchami (4, 5) in Pausha (December) Saptami and Ashtami (7, 8) in Margashirsa (December) and Ashtami and Navami (8. 9) in Chaitra (March) are given the name of Zero tithis in both the Pakshas. In the dark half of the month of Kartika (November) Ashadha (July). Phalguna (February) Jyeshtha (May) and Magha (January) the Panchami tithi (5), the Shashthi (6), the Chaturthi (4) the Chaturdashi (14) and Panchami (5) are respectively the zero tithis and so are respectively the Chaturdashi (14), the Saptami (7), the Tritiya (3), the Trayodashi (13) and the Shashthi (6) in the bright half of the month.

INAUSPICIOUSNESS ARISING OUT OF THE CONJUNCTION OF TITHI AND NAKSHTRA: And in the same way if it happens that the Ashlesha Nakshtra falls on the Dwadashi Tithi, the Uttarashadha on the Pratipada (1), Anuradha on the Dwitiya (2), Makha on the Panchami (5), the three Uttaras (Uttara Phalguni, Uttara Shadha and Uttara Bhadrapada) on the Tritiya (3), Rohini on Ekadashi (11), Swati and Chitra on Trayodashi (13), Hasta and Moola on Saptami (7), Kritika on Navami (9), Poorva Bhadrapada on Ashtami (8), and Rohini on Shashthi, then the tithi is inauspicious for performing auspicious deeds.

ZERO NAKSHTRAS (STARS) IN THE MONTHS CHAITRA ETC.: The Nakshtras (stars) Rohini and Ashwini in the month of Chaitra, and Swati in Vaishakha, Uttara-shadha and Pushya in Jyeshtha, Poorva Phalguni and Dhanishtha in Ashadha, Uttarashadha and Shravana in Shravana, Shatabhisa and Rewati in Bhadrapada, Poorvabhadrapada in Asvina, Kritika and Makha in Kartika, Chitra and Vishakha in Marga shirsa, Aridra, Ashwini and Hasta in Pausha, Shravana and Moola in Magha and Bharani and Jyeshtha in Phalguna- are called or named as Zero Nakshtras (stars). If an auspicious deed is done in such Zero Nakshtras it causes loss of wealth.

ZERO SIGNS IN THE MONTHS CHAITRA ETC.: In the months of Chaitra, Vaishakha, Jyeshtha, Ashadha, Shravana, Bhadrapada, Ashvina, Kartika, Marga shirsa, Pausha, Magha and Phalguna, the signs respectively of Aquarius, Pisces, Taurus, Gemini, Aries, Virgo, Scorpio, Libra, Sagittarius, Cancer, Capricorn and Leo are zero signs.

ZERO ASCENDANTS (DAGDHA LAGNAS IN ODD TITHIS)
In both the Pakshas, the Shukla and the Krishna Pakshas in the odd tithis beginning from Pratipada, Libra and Capricorn on Pratipada (1), Leo and Capricorn on Tritiya (3), Gemini and Virgo on Panchami (5), Sagittarius and Cancer on Saptami... Pisces on Trayodashi (13), are named as zero signs. Auspicious deeds performed in these Ascendants cause harm and bring undesirable effects.

LEAVING OF EVIL COMBINATIONS IN DOING GOOD DEEDS: The Zero tithis of the month, and whatever zero signs there are, should be left out (and on these no auspicious deed should be performed) in Madhya Desha (Central India, a particular region in India). In other regions these are not bad for doing auspicious deeds.

COMBINATIONS WHICH ARE TO BE LEFT OUT IN DOING ALL AUSPICIOUS DEEDS: The Panchami Tithi (5) with the Hasta Nakshtra falling on Sunday, Saptami (7) with Ashwini on Tuesday, Shashthi (6) with Mrigasira on Monday, Ashtami (8) with Anuradha on Wednesday, Dashmi (10) with Rewati on Friday, Navami (9) with Pushya on Thursday and Ekadashi (11) with Rohini on Saturday-these combinations are to be avoided in doing all auspicious deeds.

YOGAS (COMBINATIONS) WHICH ARE TO BE AVOIDED IN ENTERING NEW HOUSE. TRAVELLING AND MARRYING The rise of Ashwini Nakshtra on Tuesday, of Rohini on Saturday and Pushya Nakshtra on Thursday-these combinations are to be avoided respectively for entering newly constructed House. travelling and marrying

METHOD OF FINDING OUT THE ANANDA ETC. yogas: If Ananda etc. yogas are to be known on Sunday count from Ashwini to the Nakshtra on Sunday, if these are to be known on Monday count from Mrigshira to the Nakshtra on Monday, if on Tuesday from Ashlesha, on Wednesday from Hasta, on Thursday from Anuradha, on Friday from Uttarashadha and, on Saturday from Shatbhisa (Abhijit also).

SARVARTHA SIDDHI YOGA: If there is on Sunday Hasta, Moola, Uttaraphalguni, Uttarashadha, Uttarabhadrapada, Pushya or Ashwini Nakshtra; on Monday, Shravana, Rohini, Mrigshira, Pushya or Anuradha; on Tuesday, Ashwini, Uttarabhadrapada, Kritika or Ashlesha; on Wednesday, Rohini, Anuradha, Hasta, Kritika or Mrigshira; on Thursday, Revati, Anuradha, Ahswini, Punarvasu, or Pushya; on Friday, Revati, Anuradha, Ashwini, Punarvasu and Shravana and; on Saturday, Shravana, Rohini or Swati Nakshtra, then, there is, according to the ancient writers on Astrology, the Sarvaratha Siddhi yoga on these days.

RAVI YOGA If by counting from that Nakshtra in which the Sun is situated to that one in which the Moon is situated there comes any of the number 4, 6, 9, 10, 13, 20, then the yoga that is formed in this way is Ravi yoga which is the destroyer of all inauspiciousness

UTPAATADI YOGA (UTPAATA, MRITYU, KANA AND SIDDHA YOGA.): On Sunday from Vishakha Nakshtra, on Monday from Purva Shadha, on Tuesday from Dhanishtha, on Wednesday from Revati, on Thursday from Rohini, on Friday from Pushya and, on Saturday from Uttaraphalguni, four Nakshtras from each onwards there are respectively the Utpaata, Mrityu, Kana and Siddha yogas The effects of these yogas are also according to their names

The inauspicious yogas forming due to the conjunction of tithi (Hindi date) and day, of tithi and Nakshtra, of Nakshtra and day and of tithi, day and Nakshtra are evil causing, and therefore should be rejected only in the countries or regions of the Punjab, Bengal and Nepal.

The Lagna or the Ascendant and the Navamsha occupied by the Moon and the malefic planets (the emaciated Moon, the Sun, Mars, and Saturn), the third part of a Ghati or 20 Palas (4 minutes) before and after mid day and mid night-these are to be rejected in doing all the auspicious deeds. Similarly, the Navamsha of a malefic planet, three days before an eclipse, seven days after a portent (like an earthquake etc.) and an eclipse and the whole day on which an auspicious portent occurs—these should also be avoided in doing, all auspicious deeds. And the Nakshtra cleaved by planets, the Nakshtra in which there is the planetary war and the Nakshtra in which there is some Utpaata or portent---these three Nakshtras are to be rejected for six months in doing all the auspicious deeds.

The Nakshtra in which there is the full eclipse of the Sun is to be rejected for six months, for 3 months if there is the half eclipse, for one month if there is the one fourth part eclipse. If the eclipsed Sun or Moon sets then three days before the eclipse, and if the eclipsed Sun or Moon rises then three days after it, no auspicious deed is to be done. And if there is the half eclipse at other time than the time of rising or setting then 3 days before and 3 days after and the full day of the eclipse, should be avoided for doing all auspicious deeds

The Nakshtra at the time of birth, the month of the birth, the date of the birth, Vyatipata, Bhadra, Vaidhriti yoga, Amavasya (the 30th Tithi of the month), the day of the death of father and mother, the tithi that has not occurred. the tithi that has been added, the month that has not occurred, the month that has been added, Kulika, Ardhayama and, Pata-these are to be rejected while doing an auspicious deed, and the 3 ghatis of the beginning of the Vishkambha and Vajra yoga should also be rejected.

THE GHATIS OF PARIDHA ETC YOGAS THAT ARE TO BE REJECTED. The first half of the Paridha Yoga, the first five Ghatis of Shubha yoga, the first 6 Ghatis of Ganda and Ati Ganda Yoga and the first 9 Ghatis of Vyaghata yoga-these should be re- jected in doing all auspicious deeds. (The remaining Ghatis are good effects giving).

The 4th, 6th, 8th, 9th, 12th and 14th-these tithis of both the Pakshas should be rejected in doing an auspicious deed. The first 8,9,14,25,10 and 5, Ghatis respectively of these tithis are to be rejected in doing all auspicious deeds. The remaining Ghatis of these tithis are auspicious and good-effects giving.

THE WAY TO FIND OUT KULIKA, KAL-BELA, YAMA-GHANTA AND KANTAKA INAUSPICIOUS MUHURTAS: Count the number from the day on which you want to find out the four inauspicious Muhurtas Kulika etc to respectively Saturday, Wednesday, Thursday, and Tuesday. The numbers arrived at in this way are to be doubled and that will give you respectively Kulika, Kalbela, Yama Ghanta and Kantaka yogas. Notes Suppose you want to find out Kulika etc yogas on Sunday Counting from Sunday to Saturday gives you 7 When this number is doubled it will give 14 So the 14th Muhurta will be Kulika Similarly, the number arrived at when counting from Sunday to Wednesday is 4 When it is doubled it gives 8 So the 8th Muhurta will be Kalbela The same method is to be used in finding out these Muhurtas on other days also. If Journey is done in the above said Muhurtas there may be the death of the native. if marriage is performed his daughter may become widow; and in Vrata bandha there occurs Brahmavadha. that is deprivation of the knowledge of Vedas etc. According to the view of Vashistha these 4 Muhurtas have not been regarded inauspicious at night. DETAILS OF BHADRA: In the Shukla Paksha or the bright half of the month there is Bhadra on the 8th and 15th tithis in the first half part of the tithi; and Bhadra is there also on the 4th and the 11th tithis in the latter half part of these tithis. Again, in the Krishna Paksha or the Dark half of the month there is Bhadra on the 3rd and the 10th tithis in the latter half part of these tithis; and Bhadra is there also on the 7th and the 14th tithis in the first half part of these tithis.

In the bright half of the month on the above said Bhadra tithis (8th, 15th, 4th and 11th tithis) in the right order of the tithis that is 4th, 8th, 11th and 15th tithis respectively 5 Ghatis at the beginning of the 5th, 2nd, 7th and 4th Prahara; and in the dark half of the month on the above said Bhadra tithis (3rd, 10th, 7th and the 14th tithis) in the right order of the tithis, that is 3rd, 7th, 10th and 14th tithis respectively 5 Ghatis at the beginning of the 8th, 3rd, 6th and 1st Prahara, there is the mouth of Bhadra. This Mouth is inauspicious. In the same way in the bright half of the month in the above said tithi order, the 3 ghatis at the beginning of the 8th, 5th, 6th and 3rd Prahara; and in the dark half of the month on the above said Bhadra tithis, in the right order of tithis 3 Ghatis at the beginning of the 7th, 2nd, 5th and 4th Prahara, there is the tail of Bhadra. This tail is auspicious. If the Bhadra of the last half of the tithi is in the day and that of the first half of the tithi is in the night, it is auspicious.

The order of the mouth of Bhadra in the tithis Chaturthi (the 4th Hindi tithi) etc. is as follows: The mouth of Bhadra is in the 5 ghatis of the beginning of the 5th Prahara (the number of the West direction), 2nd (the number of the Agni Kona), 7th (the number of the North direction), 4th (the number of Nairirtya Kona), 8th (the number of the Ishaan Kona), 3rd (the number of the South direction), 6th (the number of the Vayavya kona) and 1st (the number of the East direction) Prahara. There is the tail of Bhadra in the 3 ghatis of the ending of the 4th Prahara from the Prahara of a tithi in which there is its mouth.

When Jupiter and Venus are in old age, in the combustion stage or in childhood stage and when there is the ‘Kshaya’ (the month that has not occurred) Month or the Malla (additional month) Month, the following things should not be performed; the building and the using of a small well, garden, tank, well and house: the beginning and ending of a vrata (fast), coming in of a newly wedded wife, Mahadaana, some yajna, Ashtaka Shraddha, Godan (the Keshanta Samskara of a Brahmachari) eating newly grown grains, water tank, the first Shrawanikarma, Vedavrata, Neelvrashotsarga, Atipanna Samaskara (the jat Karmadi Samskaras of children which have not been performed in proper time), Deva Pratishtha (performing the life giving ceremony of a god) learning the first lesson from the guru (teacher), putting on the Sacred thread, marriage, the first cutting of hair, the first visit to a god or the first going to a place of pilgrimage, renunciation of the world, Agnihotra (or burning the sacred fire), the first visit to a king, coronation, journey, yajna of four months, Samavartana. piercing the ear and the testing of some celestial objects.

Notes: Jupiter and Venus are said to be old before they are combust and they are in their infancy after rising.

All the deeds that should not be performed when Jupiter is combust (these are described in Shlokas 46 and 47) should also be left out (postponed) when Jupiter is in the sign of Leo or Capricorn. According to some learned Astrologers all these deeds are also to be left out when Jupiter is retrograde and is Atichari. In the same way all these deeds are to be left out during the period when Jupiter and the Sun remain in the same sign or when a Paksha (fortnight or one half of the month) is of 13 days. During these periods things made of ivory or elephant teeth (tusk) and jewels having gems studded in them are not to be got made and also not to be worn.

LEAVING OUT THE PERIOD IN WHICH JUPITER IS IN THE SIGN OF LEO IN THREE WAYS: First, when Jupiter is there in the sign of Leo and he is also in the Navamsha of Leo, marriage etc. are not to be performed. (This Navamsha, of Leo extends from 4-13° 20' to 4-16°–40'). Auspicious deeds like marriage etc are to be left out not at other places than at those that are there from the Northern Bank of Godavari to the Southern Bank of the Northern Ganga (that is, the regions of Central India, Madhya Bharata and Rajasthan). If the Sun is in the sign of Aries, then there is no defect of Jupiter's situation in the sign of Leo. Notes Geographically Rajasthan Gujarat. Madhya Pradesh, some Northern part of Maharashtra, and some Southern Parts of Urissa, Uttarapradesh and Bihar fall in between the Ganga and the Godavari

The leaving out of the defective period when the Sun is in the sign of Aries is confirmed in Jyotirnibandha also
The girl married when the Sun is in the sign of Aries or when Jupiter is in the sign of Leo is of an excellent conduct, is truthful and is endowed with jewels, diamonds happiness and fame.

The period in which Jupiter is situated in the sign of Leo is to be rejected in all countries (regions) in the five quarters from Magha Nakshtra, that is, four quarters of the Magha Nakshtra and one quarter of Poorvaphalguni. This period is not defective and not to be rejected in the remaining four quarters (that is 3 quarters of Poorvaphalguni and one of Uttara Phalguni Nakshtra) except in the region between the rivers Ganga and Godawari. But if the Sun is in the sign of Aries in this region also (the region between Ganga and Godawari) marriage and engagement etc are auspicious. The period when Jupiter is in the sign of Leo should be rejected while performing auspicious deeds in all places in the region of Kalinga (on the Southern Bank of the river Vaitarni of Urissa and on the Northern Bank of the river Krishna to the regions of Raj Mahendri Vishakhapattana and Ganjaam district) Gaur (from Madhya or Central Bengal to the Northern limit of Urissa or Bardwana) and in that of Gurjars or Gujarat. (In these regions the period when Jupiter is in the sign of Leo is not to be rejected even when the Sun is in the sign of Aries).

AVOIDANCE OF THE PERIOD FOR PERFORMING AUSPICIOUS DEEDS WHEN JUPITER IS IN THE SIGN OF CAPRICORN OR WHEN HE IS IN HIS FALL: In the region to the east of the river Reva (or Narmada which flows in the regions of Jabalpur etc.), to the west of the river Gandaki (which rises from the Himalayas and joins the river Ganga near Patna city of the State of Bihar after flowing to the west of Nepal; this river is called by different names in different places such as at some places it is called Narayani, at others Shaalgrami and at others Gandaki), to the north and the south of the river Sonbhadra (this river joins the river Ganga at Patna) auspicious deeds may be performed when Jupiter is in his fall or he is in the sign of Capricorn, the performance of such deeds should not be avoided; but auspicious deeds are not to be performed and should be avoided in the regions of Konkana (the region of Southern India which comprises Canara, Ratnagiri, Kolava, Bombay, Thana etc.), Magadha (the Southern part of the modern state of Bihar), Gaur region (Central Bengal and Urissa), the Sindha region (Kutchh and Bahavalpura Vela which is now called Bombay).

THE LUPTA SAMVATSARA AND ITS AVOIDANCE IN PERFORMING AUSPICIOUS DEEDS If Jupiter is Atichari in oth- er signs except those of Taurus, Aries, Pisces and Aquarius, and if after becoming retrograde he does not move back to the former sign (the sign in which he has become Atichari) then that Varsha (the Guru Varsha related to the former sign which has been crossed due to his being Atichari) will be called Lupta-Samvatsar (or Mahatichaar). This Lupta samvatsar is to be completely rejected in performing auspicious deeds.

VAAR PRAVARTI (THE TIME AT WHICH A DAY BEGINS: One fourth (1/4) is to be obtained of the distance (in yojanas; a yojana is a measure of distance) of one's own city from the cities or the regions through which the Prime meridian line has passed (According to the ancient sages the cities and the regions through which it has passed are Kalicut, Sholapur, Ujjain, Kurukshetra, Jalagaon, Indore, Sawai Madhopur, Jaipur, Pilani, Ludhiana, Jammu etc), whether one's own city is situated to the west or to the east of this line. This one fourth part is to be subtracted from the number of these very yojanas. The figure which is arrived at after subtraction is supposed to be so many palas and these palas are added to 15 ghatis (If one's own city is to the west of the Prime Meridian line, then these Palas are added to 15 ghatis; if it is to the east then these are to be subtracted from 15 ghatis. How much less the number of the ghatis and palas obtained in this way is from the Dinaardha (Half of the Dinmaana) of one's own city that much number of ghatis and palas will be the Vaar Pravarti after the rising of the Sun. If the number is greater, then Vaar Pravarti will be as much before the rising of the Sun as this number is greater than the Dinaardha of one's own city. Notes Here is an example to know the Vaarpravarti. Suppose Varanasi is at a distance of 63 yojanas (1 yojana = 5 kosha and one kosha = about 1¼ miles) from the Prime Meridian Line. One fourth part of it will be 63 ÷ 4 = 15°- 45. This figure when it is subtracted from 63 gives 47 - 15 These are palas and these are subtracted from 15 ghatis. The remainder comes to be 14/12/45 Then suppose in a given year, in a given month and on a given day the Dinaardha is 15 ghatis and 24 palas. We want to know the Vaar Pravarti of this day. Here we find that our remainder is less than the Dinaardha. The difference between the two is 1/11/15. Therefore, on this particular day the Vaar Pravesh occurred 1/11/15 (one ghati, 11 palas and 15 vipalas) after the rising of the Sun. If this difference comes to be zero then Vaar Pravesh occurs just at the rising of the Sun.

The ghatis and palas of the Ishta Kaala (the time the Kaala Hora of which is to be known) from the time when there is the Vaar Pravriti are doubled and the figure so obtained is to be put at two places. The doubled ghatis and palas of one place are to be divided by 5. The remainder after dividing is to be subtracted from the doubled ghatis and palas and 1 is to be added to it and the figure so obtained will give the Kaal Hora of the Ishta Kaal. If the total comes to be more than 7, then it is divided by 7 and the remainder will be the number of the day the lord of which will be the Kaal Horesh (counting from the day on which the Kaal Hora is to be known).

Notes: Suppose it is to be known as to who will be the Horapati or Horesh at 6 Ishta ghati on Monday, that is Kaal Horesh is to be known after 6 ghatis from Vaar Pravarti. Then according to the Rule Ishta ghati is doubled which gives 12. This figure is put at two places. the figure of the second place is divided by 5. The remainder which is 2 is to be subtracted from the doubled Ishta ghati 12 which gives 10. Then by adding 1 to 10 we get 11. This figure is divided by 7 as it is more than 7. The remainder after dividing comes to be 4. Counting from the Lord of Monday (the Moon) the Lord of the 4th day, Thursday (Jupiter) will be the Kaal Horesh.

There are 24 Horas in every day as 2½ ghatis = 1 Hora, that is, one Hora is equal to 1 Hour. The First Hora will be of the day which is there on that particular day. Thus on Sunday the First Hora will be of the Sun, the Lord of Sunday.

The deed which has been advised in the Shastras to be performed on a particular day may be done (on any day) in the Kaal Hora of the Lord of that day; the deed which has been advised to be done in a particular Nakshtra, that may be done in the Tithyamsha or Muhurta or in the 15th part of the Lord of that Nakshtra (There are 15 Muhurtas in a day). These are called Swami Tithyamsha. A Tithyamsha is equal to the 15th part of Dinmaan and is considered to be the part of the Nakshtra. The consideration of the defect of Vaar Shoola and Nakshtra Shoola is also to be made both in the Hora and in the Muhurta; and Parighdanda (the special defect of the time of a journey) according to Shloka 36 of Chapter 11) is not to be violated even in the Muhurta of the Nakshtra.

The 3rd and the 15th (the Purnima) Tithi of the bright half of the month of Chaitra, the 15th and the 12th tithi of the bright half of the month of Kartika: the 10th and the 15th tithi of the bright half of the month of Ashadha: the 15th tithi of the bright half of the month of Jyestha; the 15th tithi of the bright half of the month of Phalguna; the ninth tithi of the bright half of the month of Ashwin, the 7th tithi of the bright half of the month of Magha: the 11th tithi of the bright half of the month of Pausha; the 3rd Tithi of the bright half of the month of Bhadrapada; and the 30th (Amavasya) and the 8th tithi of the dark half of the month of Shravana-these 14 tithis are tithis of Manu etc. On these tithis begin respectively the 14 Manus.

LORDS OF THE NAKSHTRAS: Nasatya (Both Ashwini Kumaras) Yama, Agni, Brahma, Chandrama, Shiva, Aditi (Dev mata), Brahaspati, Sarpa, Pitara, Bhaga (a particular Sun), Aryama (a particular Sun), Ravi, Twashta (Vishwakarma), Vayu, Shakragni (Indra and Agni), Mitra (a particular Sun) Indra, Niririti (Rakshasa), Ksheer (Jala or water), Vishwedeva, Vidhi (Vidhata) Govinda (Vishnu), Vasu, Varuna, Ajcharana (a particular Sun), Ahir-budhanya (a particular Sun) and Poosha (a particular Sun), these are respectively the names of the Lords of the Nakshtras Ashwini etc.

THE NAKSHTRAS, STHIR OR DHRUWA (FIXED) AND THE THINGS WHICH SHOULD BE DONE IN THEM: The three Uttaras (Uttara Phalguni, Uttarashadha and Uttara-Bhadrapada) Rohini and the day of Sunday these are called Sthir or Dhruwa. In these Nakshtras and on this day things of fixed and permanent nature, things concerning one’s house, sowing of seeds things or rites done for getting peace and the planting of small garden etc. can be auspiciouly done.

THE NAKSHTRAS CHARA (Movable) ETC. AND THE THINGS WHICH SHOULD BE DONE IN THEM: The Nakshtras Swati, Punarvasu, Shravana, Dhanistha, Satbhisha and the day of Monday-these are called Chara and Chala. In these Nakshtras and on this day such things as riding an elephant etc. walking in a garden and things which are too be done in the Nakshtras called Laghu may be auspiciously performed.

THE NAKSHTRAS UGRA-KRUR (CRUEL) ETC. AND THE THINGS WHICH SHOULD BE PERFORMED IN THEM: The Nakshtras, the three Poorvas (Poorva Phalguni, Poorvashadha, and Poorva Bhadrapada) Bharani, and Magha and the day of Tuesday these are called ugra and Krur (of strong and Malefic Nature). In these Nakshtras and on this day ambush (killing some one), burning (of the House etc.), deception (cheating some one), poisoning (giving poison to some one or to one's own self), using weapons (using or making weapons)-these things may be effectively done. And the things which are to be performed in the Nakshtras called 'Daruna' (Horrible) may also be performed in those called Ugra, Krur etc.

THE NAKSHTRAS MISHRA (MIXED) AND SADHARANA (ORDINARY) ETC. AND THE THINGS WHICH SHOULD BE PERFORMED IN THEM: The Nakshtras Vishakha and Kritika and the day of Wednesday are called Mishra (Mixed) and Sadharana (ordinary) (of mixed and ordinary nature). In these Agnihotra (the burning of the sacred fire), deeds of adulteration (mixing) Vrashotsarga (giving of an ox for getting one's desire fulfilled) may be auspiciously done. And the things which are to be done in the Nakshtras called ugra (cruel) may also be effectively performed in them.

THE NAKSHTRAS URDHWA (HAVING MOUTHS UP-WARD), ADHA (HAVING MOUTHS DOWN WARD) AND THOSE WHICH HAVE TIRYAKA OR CURVED MOUTHS AND THE THINGS WHICH SHOULD BE PERFORMED IN THEM: Moola. Ashlesha, the Nakshtras which are called Mishra or mixed (Vishakha and Kritika), those which are called Ugra (Poorva Phalguni, Poorvashadha, Poorva Bhadrapada, Bharani, Magha)-these are called Adhomukha Nakshtras (The Nakshtras having their mouths downwards). Ardra, Pushya, Shravana, Dhanishtha, Shatabhisha, and the Nakshtras which are called Dhruwa (Uttara Phalguni, Uttarashadha, Uttarabhadrapada, Rohini)-these are called Urdhavamukhi Nakshtras (or the Nakshtras which have their mouths upwards). And Anuradha, Hasta, Swati, Poonarvasu, Jyesha and Ashwini, these are called Tiryaka Mukha Nakshtras (or the Nakshtras which have their mouths curved). It is auspicious to do the same kind of things in a Nakshtra that are like it.

THE NAKSHTRAS MRIDU (DELICATE) AND MAITRA (FRIENDLY) AND THE THINGS WHICH SHOULD BE PERFORMED IN THEM: The four Nakshtras Mrigshira, Rewati, Chitra and Anuradha and the day of Friday are called Mridu (delicate and Benefic) and Maitra (friendly). In these the learning and the singing of songs, getting clothes prepared and wearing them, playing games, the things relating to friends, getting jewels made and wearing them may be auspiciously done.

THE NAKSHTRAS CALLED TEEKSHNA (SHARP) AND DARUNA (HORRIBLE) AND THE THINGS WHICH SHOULD BE PERFORMED IN THEM: The Nakshtras Moola, Jyeshtha, Ardra, and Ashlesha and the day of Saturday, these are called Tikshna (sharp) and Daruna (horrible). In these Abhichaar Karma (Marana or killing some one, Mohan or hypnotizing some one, Uchchatan (distraction) etc., these Tantrika experiments), deeds of ambush, and of horror, causing difference among friends etc. (that is, causing quarrel by backbiting) and training and tying of an animal, these things may be effectively and auspiciously done.

THE MUHURTA FOR WEARING CLOTHES ETC. Revati, the Nakshtras called Dhruwa, Ashwini, Hasta, Chitra, Swati, Vishakha, Anuradha, Dhanishtha. Pushya and Punarvasu these Nakshtras... Rikta Tithis (4/9/14), the days of Saturday, Monday and Tuesday-in the Nakshtras tithis and days except these (the above mentioned ones), it is not proper to wear Coral, things made of tusk (elephant teeth) Sankha, gold and clothes (that is, these things should be worn on the Nakshtras, tithis and days mentioned above and not on others) And in the Nakshtras called Dhruwa, Punarvasu and Pushya, a woman whose husband is living should not wear new clothes. To wear red clothes Tuesday has been considered to be auspicious.

Notes: The Nakshtras Punarvasu, Pushya, and those which are called Dhruwa have been specially recommended for wearing new clothes. These Nakshtras are not recommended for a woman who is fortunate in having her husband alive because if she wears new clothes in these Nakshtras she remains deprived of having her husband's company (sexual intercourse). For men and widowed women wearing clothes etc. in these Nakshtras is not prohibited. It is obligatory for woman whose husband is alive that she should not take bath on the day on which falls the Shatbhisha Nakshtra. Shri Chandeshwar says in this connection.

THE EFFECTS WHEN A NEW CLOTH IS BURNT, TORN AND SOAKED IN MUD: The clothes (so burnt etc.) be divided into 9 parts. Then it is to be imagined that there are gods in the four corners, demons in the three parts of the middle and men in the remaining parts of the sides. If the new cloth is burnt or is torn or is soaked in mud in the part of the demons then it is inauspicious. If it so happens in the part either of the men or of the gods, then it is auspicious. If it so happens in the borders of the part of all the three, then it is inauspicious.

THE AUSPICIOUS AND INAUSPICIOUS TIME FOR THE PERSON WHO BURNS THE DUMMY: The person who performs the 'Pret Kriya', should not do such rites as the cremation rite etc in the 'Janama' and Pratyari Taras (These have been referred to and described in the 'Gochara Prakarana') and when the moon is there in the Houses of 4/8/12 from his Janama Rashi or the sign in which the Moon is situated. The performing of 'Pret Kriya Karma is medium effects-giving (for the person doing it if it is performed in the 12 Nakshtras of Anuradha, Poorvaphalguni, Punarvasu, in those called Dhruwa (Uttaraphalguni, Uttarashadha, Uttarabhadrapada and Rohini) in those of Vishakha, Mrigshira, Chitra and Dhanishtha. The Pret Kriya is auspicious for the person performing it on the days of Sunday, Monday and Thursday and in the Nakshtras of Shravana, Hasta, Swati, Ashwini and Pushya. Consideration has been done with regard to the auspiciousness of the cremation of Dummy rite etc. The performing of these is not to be done during the time of 'Ashaucha' (The period of Pataka: After someone's death in the family a fixed period is regarded as unholy for the members of that family and in this period the performing of worship, recitation of Mantras and other auspicious deeds are not done, their performing is rejected).

The planting of creepers and trees is auspicious in the Nakshtras of Vishakha, Moola, Shatbhisha, the Nakshtras called Mridu, Dhruwa and Kshipra. The seeing of Royalty is auspicious in the Nakshtras of Shravana, Dhanistha, the Nakshtras called Mridu, Dhruwa and Kshipra. Preparing and drinking of wine is auspicious in the Nakshtra of Shatbhisha, the Nakshtras called Tikshna and Ugra. The purchase and sale of cows is auspicious in the Nakshtras of Revati, Vishakha, Punarvasu, Jyestha, Shatbhisha, Dhanistha and the Nakshtras called Kshipra.

In such an auspicious ascendant when there is no planet in the 8th House, in the Nakshtra of one's own yoni (described in chapter 6) in the Nakshtras called chara it is excellent to protect animals. And in the Rikta Tithi, Ashtami (the 8th Hindi tithi) Amavasya (the 30th tithi), on Tuesday, in Shravana, Chitra and the Nakshtras called Dhruwa the going of animals (cattle) out of cow shed and their entering, bringing up in it, this is not auspicious.

MUHURTAS FOR GETTING JEWELS AND WEAPONS MADE: It is auspicious to get Jewels made on the day in which Tripushkar yoga falls (The Tripushkar yoga is formed when Bhadra Tithis (2/7/12 tithis) the days of Saturday, Tuesday and Sunday, the Nakshtras of Vishakha, Uttaraphalguni, Poorvabhadrapada, Punarvasu, Kritika and Uttarashadha-these three are joined) and in the Nakshtras called Chara, Kshipra and Dhruwa. Jewels studded with diamonds and gems should be got prepared in the other Nakshtras except the Nakshtras called Tikshna and Ugra, on Sundays and Tuesdays and in the Ascendants of Aries, Scorpio and Leo. Jewels studded with Pearls should be got prepared in the Nakshtras called Chara, Mridu, Dhruwa and Kshipra and on an auspicious day and in an auspicious Ascendant. And it is auspicious to get weapons made in the Nakshtras called Tikshna and Ugra, the Nakshtras of Ashwini, Mrigshira, Vishakha and Kritika.

THE MUHURTA OF MAKING PURCHASE AND SALE: It is inauspicious to make a sale in the Nakshtras of making purchase and to make a purchase in the Nakshtras of making sale. The Nakshtras of Revati, Shatbhisha, Ashwini, Swati, Shravana and Chitra are auspicious with regard to making purchase.

The selling of a thing is auspicious, in the three 'Poorva Nakshtras', that is Poorva Phalguni, Poorvashadha and Poorvabhadrapada, Vishakha, Kritika, Ashlesha, and Bharani Nakshtras, if benefices are there in angles and trines and malefics are in 3/6/11 Houses, there is another Ascendant except Aquarius and on auspicious tithis.

The opening of a shop is auspicious, on other tithis, days and in ascendant leaving Rikta tithis, the day of Tuesday and the Ascendant of Aquarius, in the Nakshtras called Mitra, Dhruwa and Kshipra, if Venus and the Moon are in the Ascendant, if there are no malefics in the 8/12 Houses and if there are benefics in the 2/10/11 Houses.

All the deeds relating to horses (purchasing, selling, riding and training of horses) may be auspiciously done in, the Nakshtras called Kshipra, the Nakshtras Revati, Dhanishtha, Mrigshira, Swati, Shatabhisha and Punarvasu, on other tithis and days except Rikta Tithis and the day of Tuesday. And the learned should perform all the deeds related to elephants in the Nakshtras called Mridu, Kshipra and chara.

THE MUHURTAS WITH REGARD TO COINING AND GETTING CLOTHES WASHED: It is auspicious to get a coin minted in the Nakshtras called Dhruwa, Mridu, Chara, and Kshipra, on other days except Monday and Saturday, on the tithis of Poorna and Jaya and when Jupiter and Venus are not combust, that is, they are rising. It is auspicious to get clothes washed in the Nakshtras of Dhanistha, Ashwini, Hasta, Chitra, Swati, Vishakha, Anuradha, Punarvasu and Pushya. And it is not auspicious to get clothes washed on Rikta tithis (4/9/14) tithi of a Parva (any Parva or festival) Shashthi tithi and the Shradhdha tithis of father and mother (shradhdha means feasting a Brahmin with certain rituals on the day of death in the month of Ashwin) and on the days of Saturday and Wednesday.

THE MUHURTAS WITH REGARD TO BEARING WEAPONS AND USING BED ETC.: Spear, armour, bow and arrow, dagger etc. these weapons are to be borne on tithis other than Rikta tithis (4/9/14), on the days of Friday, Thursday and Sunday, in the Nakshtras called Maitra, Dhruwa and Laghu, Punarvasu, Jyestha and Vishakha, in the sthir (fixed) Lagnas or Ascendants (2/5/8/11), if the Moon in the Ascendant is aspected by a benefic and benefic planets are situated in the Angles (1/4/7/10). The first ascending on a bed or an aasana (a mat) is auspicious in the Nakshtras called Dhruwa, Mridu and Laghu and in Shravana, Bharani, Punarvasu Nakshtras.

ANDHAKSHA, MANDAKSHA, MADHYAKSHA AND SWAKSHA NAMES OF THE NAKSHTRAS: Dhanishtha, Pushya, Rohini, Poorvashadha, Vishakha, Uttaraphalguni and Revati-these seven Nakshtras are called Andhaksha. Hasta, Uttarashadha, Anuradha, Shatabhisha, Ashlesha, Ashwini and Mrigshira-these 7 Nakshtras are named as Mandaksha. Ardra, Magha, Poorva Bhadrapada, Chitra, Jyestha, Abhijit and Bharani, these 7 Nakshtras are called Madhyaksha; Swati, Punarvasu, Shravana, Kritika, Uttara Bhadrapada, Moola and Poorvaphalguni, these 7 Nakshtras are named as Swaksha.

62 Muhurta Chinta Mani wealth lost (or stolen) in the Nakshtras named Andhaksha is gained immediately; that lost (or stolen) in those called Mandaksha is gained with efforts; that lost (or stolen) in those called Madhyaksha is heard of in or after many days to be in a distant, remote place, but it (this wealth) is not gained and; that lost (or stolen) in those named Swaksha or Sulochana is neither heard of nor gained.

THE NAKSHTRAS WHICH SHOULD BE REJECTED IN LENDING AND BORROWING AND AMASSING MONEY: The money which is lent to some one as a loan, is kept in a chest or buried under ground, is given to some one on interest or is lost in the Nakshtras named Teekshana, Mishra, Dhruwa and Ugra and the yogas of Bhadrakarana and Vyatipaata is not got back.

In the Nakshtras of Anuradha, Hasta, those called Dhruwa, and those of Dhanistha, Shatbhisha, Magha, Poorvashadha, Revati Pushya and Mrigshira; if there is Mercury or Jupiter in the Ascendant; if the Malefics are weak; if Venus is situated in the 10th House from the Ascendant and the Moon is of the watery signs (9/10/11/12), in such a Muhurta the digging of a well and a tank etc is auspicious. In the above said Nakshtras excluding Poorvashadha and Magha and including Jyeshtha Nakshtra, if there is Mercury in the Ascendant and the Moon is there in Gemini or Virgo sign and there are benefic planets in the 4th House, then the learning or the first beginning of Dancing is auspicious.

THE MUHURTA FOR SOWING SEEDS: The sowing of seeds is auspicious on the tithis and days and in the Nakshtras which have been said as auspicious for ploughing, that is, the sowing of seeds is auspicious in the Nakshtras of Moola, Magha, Swati, Dhanishtha, Uttaraphalguni, Uttarashadha, Uttara Bhadrapada, Rohini, Mrigshira, Rewati, Chitra, Anuradha, Hasta, Ashwini and Pushya and on the days of Monday, Wednesday Thursday and Friday; 8 Nakshtras from the Nakshtra in which Rahu is there are inauspicious for the sowing of seeds; three Nakshtras after it are auspicious, then one Nakshtra is inauspicious, then three Nakshtras are auspicious, then again one Nakshtra is inauspicious; and then again 3 Nakshtras are auspicious, then one Nakshtra is inauspicious, and then 3 Nakshtras are auspicious and then four Nakshtras are inauspicious. Seeds are to be sown in the auspicious Nakshtras only. This is called Rahu Chakra or Hala Chakra or the cycle of Rahu or the cycle of plough share. The Munis or thinkers have called inauspicious and auspicious the 3/8/9/8 Nakshtras from the Nakshtra in which the Sun is there in this Rahu Chakra or 'Hala Chakra', that is, the three Nakshtras before the Nakshtra in which the Sun is there are inauspicious for ploughing, then 8 Nakshtras are auspicious, then again 9 Nakshtras are inauspicious and 8 Nakshtras are auspicious.

THE MUHURTA OF LENDING AND BORROWING MONEY: The use of money (the exchange of money, depositing money in the Bank, taking LIC Policy and lending money etc) is auspicious in the Swati, Punarvasu, the Nakshtras called Mridu (Mrigshira, Rewati, Chitra and Anuradha) Vishakha, Pushya, Shravana, Dhanishtha, Shatbhisha, and Ashwini Nakshtras; in the Ascendants called chara (Movable) which are 1/4/7/10 and if there is no planet in the 9th, 5th and 8th Houses from the Ascendant. Money is not to be borrowed on Tuesday. On the day of the Sankranti of the Sun in the Vridhi yoga, in the Hasta Nakshtra and on Sunday-money borrowed at these times continues to exist in the borrower's family for ever, that is, such debt is never completely paid off and the burden of it is always there on his family; even his sons and grandsons are never relieved from this debt. Money should not be lent to any one on Wednesday.

THE MUHURTA FOR PLOUGHING: Ploughing (First ploughing at the beginning of the year or the session) has been said to be auspicious in the Nakshtras of Moola, Vishakha, Magha, in those named as 'Chara' or Movable (Swati, Punarvasu, Shravana, Dhanishtha and Shatbhisha), in all the three Uttaras and Rohini, in those called Mridu or Delicate (Mrighshira, Rewati, Chitra and Anuradha), in those called Kshipra (Hasta, Ashwini and Pushya), on days other than Sundays and Saturdays; when the Malefics (the Sun, Mars and Saturn) are weakened; when the Moon is in the Navamsha of the watery signs (4/10/11/12); when the Planets of Venus and the Moon have full strength and when Jupiter is posited in the Ascendant. There is loss in Agriculturing if ploughing is performed in the Ascendants of Leo, Aquarius, Cancer, Aries, Capricorn and Libra, on the Rikta Tithis (4/9/14) and on the Shashthi (6th) Tithi.

SHIRA CHHEDANA OR THE LETTING OUT OF BLOOD FROM VEINS (FOR PURIFICATION OF BLOOD). The Nakshtras of Chitra, Swati, Anuradha, Jyestha, Rohini, Mrigshira, Shatbhisha, those called Laghu (Hasta, Ashwini and Pushya) and Shravana and the days of Tuesday, Sunday and Thursday are auspicious for Shira Chhedana or the letting out of blood from veins. VIRECHANA AND VAMAN OR CATHARSIS AND VOMITING (Taking medicinal anema or laxative and to take medicine for vomitting for cleaning the bowels): For Virechana, the Nakshtras that have been said to be auspicious for Shiro Chhedana and the other days than those of Wednesday and Saturday are auspicious. PERFORMANCE OF RELIGIOUS RITES OR DEEDS: the performance of religious rites is proper and auspicious in the Nakshtras called Mitra (friend)-Mrigshira, Rewati, Chitra, and Anuradha-those called Kshipra-Hasta, Ashwini and Pushya-those called Chara or Movable-Swati, Punarvasu, Shravana, Dhanishtha, Shatbhisa-those called Dhruwa-Uttaraphalguni, Uttarashadha, Uttara Bhadrapada and Rohini-on Sunday and on the days of Benefic Planets, that is, on Wednesdays, Thursdays, Fridays and Mondays, if there is the Shadavarga of Mercury or Jupiter, in the Ascendant or if there is Jupiter in the Ascendant and Jupiter is strong also.

THE MUHURTA FOR REAPING CORN: Corn should be reaped in the Nakshtras called Tikshna (Moola. Jyeshtha. Ardra and Ashlesha), Poorva Bhadrapada, Hasta, Kritika, Dhanishtha, Shravana, Mrigshira, Swati, Magha, all the three Uttaras, Poorvashadha, Bharani, Chitra and Pushya, on the days other than those of Saturdays and Tuesdays and on the Tithis other than those of Rikta, and in the Ascendants that are sthir or fixed (2/5/8/11)

THE MUHURTA FOR KANAMARDANA (THRESHING THE CORN) AND DHANYA ROPANA (PLUCKING THE PLANTS OF CORN FROM ONE PLACE AND PLANTING THEM AT ANOTHER): Kanmardana or Threshing should be done in the Nakshtras of Poorvaphalguni, Uttaraphalguni, Shravana, Magha, Jyeshtha, Rohini, Moola, Anuradha and Rewati. Dhanya Ropana is auspicious in the Nakshtras of Vishakha, Poorva Bhadrapada, Moola, Rohini, Shatbhisha and Uttaraphalguni, and on other days than those of Saturday and Tuesday.

THE MUHURTA FOR THE STORAGE OF THE GRAINS AND THE INCREASING OF IT: The storage of the grains is auspicious in the Nakshtras other than those called Mishra or Mixed (Vishakha and Kritika), those called Ugra or intense (All the three Poorvas, Poorvaphalguni, Poorvashadha, and Poorva Bhadrapada. Bharani and Magha) Ardra, Ashlesha and Jyeshtha, in all the Ascendants other than those of Cancer, Aries, and Libra and on all the auspicious days. In the same way the increasing of grains by lending it on interest is good (and profit giving) in the Nakshtras called Dhruwa (All the three Uttaras, Uttara Phalguni, Uttara Shadha and Uttara Bhadrapada and Rohini) in those of Pushya, Vishakha, Jyeshtha, Ashwini and in those named as Chara or Movable (Swati, Poonarvasu, Shravana, Dhanishtha and Shatbhisha).

THE MUHURTA FOR PACIFICATION: The Beneficial rites and the pacification of the planets etc are beneficially and auspiciously performed in the Nakshtras called Kshipra (Hasta, Ashwini and Pushya), in those named as Dhruwa (All the three Uttaras, Uttara Phalguni, Uttara Shadha and Uttara Bhadrapada and Rohini), in that of Rewati, in those called ‘Chara’ or Movable (Swati, Poonarvasu, Shravana, Dhanishtha, and Shatbhisha) and in those of Anuradha and Magha, in an Ascendant in which Jupiter is in the Ascendant, the Sun is in the 10th House and the Moon is in the 4th House. The performing of pacification of the planets is not auspicious when Jupiter and Venus are combust. But the pacification of ‘Nimitta’ (seeing of Dhooma Ketu when he rises, seeing the Kak Maithun or copulating of crows, falling the occurrence of an eclipse in the Nakshtras of the birth etc) may be performed even when Jupiter and Venus are combust.

THE MUHURTA FOR DOING HAVANA OR YAJNA (BURNING SACRED FIRE): In the three Nakshtras each from the Nakshtra of the Sun to that of the Moon, the Planets respectively of the Sun, Mercury, Venus, Saturn, Moon, Mars, Jupiter, Rahu and Ketu are the Sharers of the ahuti of the Havana (Ahuti—the spices etc that are poured into fire in one lot). The Ahuti of the Havana is inauspicious in the Nakshtra which belongs to a Malefic Planet.

THE ABODE OF LIVING OF FIRE IN THE HAVANA AND THE AUSPICIOUS AND INAUSPICIOUS EFFECTS OF IT: One should be added to the 'Tithi' (the 'Ishta Tithi or the desired Tithi from the Shukla Pratipada or the I Tithi of the Shukla Paksha) and then the number of the day (the number from Sunday) is to be added to it and the Sum is to be divided by 4. If the reminder is 3 or 0, then the abode of the Fire is on the Earth and by doing the Havana on that day the performer gets happiness; if the remainder comes to be 1, the abode of the Fire is in Heaven and by doing Havana on that day there is the loss of life; if the remainder comes to be 2, the abode of the Fire is in the Paatal or the Hades (the underworld) and by doing Havana on that day there is the loss of wealth.

THE FAVOURABLE OR SUITABLE LAGNA OR 'ASCENDANT FOR DOING ALL THE ORDINARY AUSPICIOUS DEEDS: The beginning of all the auspicious deeds has been regarded as proper and excellent if there is any sign in the Ascendant of the signs of Upachaya Houses, that is, the 3rd, the 6th, the 10th and the 11th House from the Natal Ascendant and from the sign in which there is the Moon that is, the Janama Rashi of the person concerned, and there should be no planet in the 8th and the 12th House (that is, the 8th and 12th Houses from the Ascendant are 'Shuddha' or without any planet); if there is the conjunction or aspect of the Benefic Planets on the Ascendant; and if the Moon is also there in the Upachaya signs (3/6/10/11) from the Ascendant.

THE EFFECTS OF THE BEGINNING OF A DISEASE AS PER THE DIFFERENCE OF NAKSHTRAS: The patient who contracts or gets fever in the 7 Nakshtras of Swati, Jyeshtha, Poorvaphalguni, Poorvashadha, Poorvabhadrapada, Ardra and Ashlesha, is subjected to death. If the fever is contracted in the Nakshtras of Rewati and Anuradha, it (the fever) remains for a long time; if it (the fever) is contracted in those of Bharani, Shravana, Shatabhisha and Chitra, for 11 days; if in those of Vishakha, Hasta, Dhanishtha, for 15 days; if in the 3 Nakshtras of Moola, Kritika and Ashwini, for 9 days; if in those of Uttarabhadrapada, Uttaraphalguni, Pushya, Punarvasu and Rohini, for 7 days; and if in those of Mrigashira, Uttarashadha, for one month. If a person is bitten by a snake in the 7 Nakshtras of Bharani, Ashlesha, Moola, those named as Mishra or Mixed (Kritika, Vishakha, Ardra and Magha) he (the person) is subjected to death.

THE COMBINATION WHICH LEADS TO IMMEDIATE DEATH AT THE BEGINNING OF THE DISEASE: If the disease has begun in the Nakshtras of Ardra, Ashlesha, Jyeshtha, Shatabhisha, Bharani, Poorvaphalguni, Poorvashadha, Poorva Bhadrapada, Vishakha, Dhanishtha and Kritika, on the days of Sunday, Tuesday and Saturday and on the Tithis of 4/9/14/12/6, the diseased person dies soon.

ing of a cot or stringed bed and making thatches for a house should

THE YOGAS OF TRIPUSHKARA AND DWIPUSHKARA: If on the days of Saturday, Tuesday and Sunday there are the Nakshtras of Vishakha, Uttaraphalguni, Poorvabhadrapada, Punarvasu, Kritika and Uttarashadha, and if on these days there are the Bhadra Tithis also (2/7/12 Tithis) then due to the conjunction of these three-days, Nakshtras and Tithis, there occurs the 'TRIPUSHKARA YOGA'. This 'Tri Pushkara Yoga' (the combination of 3) gives three fold effect in the death, in the destruction and in the increase (the meaning is that if there is the 'Tripushkara yoga' and if there is death in someone's house, then 3 persons will die in his house, if there is the destruction of something in someone's house in this yoga, then there will occur the destruction of 3 things, and if in this yoga there is the profit of one thing to someone, then there will be to him the profit of three things). And the conjunction of these 3, the days of Saturday, Tuesday, and Sunday; the Nakshtras of Dhanishtha, Chitra and Mrigshira; and the Bhadra Tithis (2/7/12 Tithis)-Causes the occurrence of the DWIPUSHKARA YOGA. This yoga gives two fold effect.

THE CONSIDERATION OF ABHUKTA MOOLA: According to Brahmarishi Narada the last four Ghatis of the Nakshtra of Jyeshtha and the first four Ghatis of that of Moola, these 8 Ghatis form the 'Abhukta Moola'. Brahmarishi Vashishtha has said that it is the last one Ghati of the Nakshtra of Jyeshtha and the first two Ghatis of that of Moola (the 3 Ghatis combined) which form the 'Abhuktamoola'. But according to Acharya Brahaspati the "Abhuktamoola" is formed by the last half Ghati of the Nakshtra of Jyeshtha and the first half Ghati of that of Moola.

It is the opinion of some unknown Acharya (teacher of Astrology) that 'Abhuktamoola' is formed by the first eight ghatis of the Nakshira of Moola and the last 5 ghatis (these 13 ghatis combined) of that of Jyeshtha. The native born in the 'Abhuktamoola' should be given up or left or the father should not see its face for eight years.

There is the destruction (death) of the native's father if the native is born in the first quarter of the Nakshtra of Moola; that of the native's mother, if in the 2nd quarter; there is the loss of wealth, if in the 3rd quarter; and the birth is auspicious if it occurs in the 4th quarter. And if Shanti Anushthana or Pacification of the defective birth is performed then it (the birth) is auspicious in all the quarters. The effects are reversed if the birth occurs in the different quarters of the Nakshtra of Ashlesha, that is, it (the birth) is auspicious if it occurs in the First quarter, it causes the loss of wealth, if in the 2nd one; it causes the death of the native's mother, if in the 3rd Quarter and; that of the native's father, if in the 4th Quarter.

The Nakshtra of Moola resides or lives in Heaven in the months of Ashadha, Bhadrapada, Ashwin and Magha; on the earth in those of Shravana, Kartika, Chaitra and Pausha; in Pataal or the Hades or the Underworld in those of Phalguna, Margashirsha, Vaishakha and Jyestha. The inauspicious effects occur in the place where the Nakshtra of Moola resides or lives.

The birth of a child occurring in the 'Gandanta' (Tithi Gandanta, Nakshtra Gandanta, and Lagna Gandanta) in the Nakshtra of Jyeshtha; in the yogas of Shoola, Mahapaata, Parigha, Vyaghaata, and Ganda; in the event of Tithi Kshaya; on a Sankranti; in Vyatipata and Vaidhriti; on the Sinivali Amavasya (the Amavasya on which the Moon is visible) and that of Kuhu (the Amavasya on which the Moon is not visible); in the Vajra yoga, on the Chaturdashi or the 14th Tithi of the Krishna Paksha or the dark half of the month; in Yamaghanta (described in 9th Shloka of the Ist Chapter of this book) in the Dagdha Yoga (described in 1/8); in the Mrityu Yoga (described in 1/30 and 1/5) in the Karana of 'Bhadra'; in the Janama Nakshtra or the Nakshtra of the birth of a brother and sister; and in that of the native's father and mother; in any of all these, is evil effects giving or inauspicious. Therefore, there should be done the Shanti or pacification of all these. All is auspicious by performing 'Shanti' or pacification.

THE NUMBER OF THE TARAS (OR STARS) OF THE NAKSHTRAS ASHWINI ETC.: There are 3 Taras in Ashwini, 3 in Bharani, 6 in Kritika, 5 in Rohini, 3 in Mrigshira, 1 in Ardra, 4 in Punarvasu, 3 in Pushya, 5 in Ashlesha, 5 in Magha, 2 in Poorvaphalguni; 2 in Uttaraphalguni, 5 in Hasta, 1 in Chitra, 1 in Swati, 4 in Vishakha, 4 in Anuradha, 3 in Jyeshtha, 11 in Moola, 2 in Poorvashadha, 2 in Uttarashadha, 3 in Abhijita, 3 in Shravana, 4 in Dhanishtha, 100 in Shatbhisha, 2 in Poorvabhadrapada, 2 in Uttarabhadrapada and 32 in Rewati.

THE SHAPES OF THE NAKSHTRAS: The shape of Ashwini is like the mouth of a horse, that of Bharani like 'Bhaga' or the Vagina of a woman, that of Kritika like a dagger, that of Rohini like a bullock cart, that of Mrigashira like the mouth of a deer, that of Ardra like a gem, that of Punarvasu like a house, that of Pushya like an arrow, that of Ashlesha like a wheel, that of Magha like a house, that of Poorvaphalguni like a stage, that of Uttaraphalguni like a bed, that of Hasta like a hand, that of Chitra like a Pearl, that of Swati like a coral, that of Vishakha like 'Torana' (A rosary of leaves hung outside a door), that of Anuradha like bali (the heap of rice), that of Jyeshtha like a Kundal (a ring or an ornament of gold or silver worn in the cars), that of Moola like the tail of a lion, that of Poorva shadha like the teeth of an elephant, that of Uttarashadha like Machan (a device to hunt a lion or to ward off birds from a field of maize), that of Abhijita like a triangle, that of Shravana, like 'Tricharana' (like the shape of Vaman, the shape which Lord Vishnu assumed to deceive Bali), that of Dhanishtha like Mridanga (an Indian Musical instrument), that of Shatbhisha like a circle, that of Poorvabhadrapada like a stage or a Machan, that of Uttarabhadrapada like two joined men, and that of Rewati like Mridanga.

THE MUHURTA FOR DIGGING AND BUILDING A TANK, FOR PLANTING A GARDEN OR AN ORCHARD AND ESTABLISHING AN IMAGE OF SOME GOD OR GODDESS: It is auspicious to begin the digging and building of a tank, the planting of a Garden or an orchard and the establishing of an image of some god or goddess in the Uttarayana of the Sun which is there from January 14 to July 16 (except in the month of Chaitra), at the rising of Venus, in the Naksthras called Mridu or delicate (Mrigashira, Rewati, Chitra and Anuradha), in those called Kshipra (Hasta, Ashwini, and Pushya), those called Chara or Movable (Swati, Punarvasu, Shravana, Dhanishtha, and Shatbhisha), in those called Dhruwa (Uttaraphalguni, Uttarashadha, Uttarabhadrapada and Rohini)-in these 16 Nakshtras in the Shukla Paksha or the bright half of the month in the Nakshtra of that god the image of whom is to be established (described in the first shloka of this very chapter), his Tithi (Tithis have been described in the 3rd shloka of Chapter 1), his Muhurta (these have been told in the Shlokas from 52 to 55 in the 6th Chapter); in all the other Tithis and Days excepting the Rikta Tithis (4/9/14) and on the day of Tuesday, at those times when the Moon and the Malefic Planets are in the Houses of 3/6/11, when the Benefic Planets are there in the other houses than those of 8 and 12. The establishing of the im- age of the Sun-God should be done in the Ascendant of Leo; that of Brahma in that of Aquarius; that of Shankar or Shiva in that of Gemini. In the Ascendants of dual natured signs (Gemini, Virgo, Sag- ittarius and Pisces) there should be the establishing of the images of the goddesses, and in the ‘Chara’ or Movable Ascendants (Aries, Can- cer, Libra and Capricorn) that of a god of lower level. Particularly, the establishing of the images of all the gods is to be done in the Ascendants of fixed signs (Taurus, Leo, Scorpio and Aquarius) The establishing of the 8 planets the Moon etc is to be done in the Nakshtra of Pushya, of the gods Ganesha, Yaksha, Sarpa (Snake) and Bhoota etc in that of Rewati, and of the gods of Jains (A Sub Religion in India) in that of Shravana.

1–1½ THE NAMES OF THE SANKRANTIS AND THEIR EFFECTS: If there is the Sankranti of the Sun in the Nakshtras named as Ugra—Poorvaphalguni, Poorvashadha, Poorvabhadrapada, Bharani and Magha that Sankranti is given the name of Ghora; this Sankranti is the giver of joy and happiness to the people of Shudra Varna or caste; if the Sankranti falls in the conjunction of the Nakshtras called ‘Laghu’ (small)—Hasta, Ashwini, Pushya and Abhijit—and of Monday, it is named as the Sankranti of Dhwankshi; it gives happiness and joy to the people of the Vaishya Varna or caste; if it happens to fall in the conjunction of those Nakshtras which are referred to as ‘Chara’ or Movable (Swati, Punarvasu, Shravana, Dhanishtha and Shatbhisha) and of the day of Tuesday, its name is ‘Mahodara’; it is the thieves who are made joyful and happy in this Sankranti; the Sankranti which happens to fall in the conjunction of the Nakshtras named as Maitra (Mrigashira, Rewati, Chitra and Anuradha) and the day of Wednesday is called by the name of ‘Mandakini’; it gives joy and happiness to the people of the Kshtriya Varna or caste; that which happens to fall in the conjunction of the Nakshtras called ‘Sthira’ or fixed (Uttaraphalguni, Uttarashadha, Uttarabhadrapada and Rohini) and of the day of Thursday is referred to as 'Manda' which is the giver of joy and happiness to the varna or caste of Brahmins; that happening to fall in the conjunction of Nakshtras named as Mishra or Mixed (Vishakha, Kritika) and of the day of Friday gets the name of 'Mishra'; it gives joy and happiness to the animals; that which falls in the conjunction of the Nakshtras named as 'Tikshna' or intense (Moola, Jyeshtha, Ardra and Ashlesha) and of Saturday is given the name of 'Rakshashi'; it gives joy and happiness to the people of 'Chandala' Caste.

If a Sankranti occurs in the first 3rd part of a day it gives pain to the Kshtriyas, if in the 2nd, to the Brahmins, if in the 3rd to the Vaishyas and if it occurs at the setting of the day it gives pain to the Shudras. If a Sankranti occurs in the first prahara of night, it destroys the Pishachas etc.; if in the 2nd one, the Rakshasas; if in the 3rd one, the Natas (actors in circus); and if in the 4th one, the guards of animals or the gopas or the cowherds. The Sankranti occurring at the time of the rising of the Sun destroys the hypocrites. The Sankranti of ‘Makara’ or Capricorn is called Uttarayana, and that of ‘Karka’ or Cancer is referred to as Dakshinayana.

THE NAMES OF THE SANKRANTIS AS PER THE DIFFERENCE OF SIGNS: The Sankranti of the signs of Sagittarius, Gemini, Virgo and Pisces is named as ‘Shadashiti Mukha’; that of the signs of Libra and Aries is called ‘Vishuwa’; and the name of that of the signs of Leo, Scorpio, Taurus and Aquarius is ‘Vishnupada’.

THE PUNYA KAALA OF A SANKRANTI: The 16 ghatis before and the 16 ghatis after the Sankranti of the Sun, that is 32 ghatis is the Punya Kaala or the holy time. If a Sankranti begins before midnight then the latter half of the previous day (from 12 o'clock to the setting of the Sun on the previous day), and if it begins after midnight, then the first half of the next day, (that is from the Sunrise to 12 o'clock on the next day) there is the Punya Kaala.

THE CONSIDERATION OF THE SPECIAL PUNYA KAALA OF A SANKRANTI: If a Sankranti begins exactly at midnight, then there is the Punya Kaala of it in both the days before and after it. If there is the Sankranti of the sign of Cancer before the rising of the Sun, then it is the previous day which is the Punya Kaala; and if there is that of the sign of Capricorn after the setting of the Sun (in the night) then the next day is the Punya Kaala.

THE MEASURE OF THE SANDHYA AND THE SPECIAL CHARACTERISTICS OF THE SANKRANTIS OF CANCER AND CAPRICORN: 3 ghatis before the half rising of the disc of the Sun is called the Sandhya (the time joining two times) of the morning; and 3 ghatis after the half setting of the disc of the Sun is referred to as the Sandhya of the evening time. If there is the Sankranti of Cancer in the Sandhya of the morning, then there is Punya Kaala in the whole day which follows this Sandhya; and if there is the Sankranti of the Capricorn in the Sandhya of the evening, then there is Punya Kaala in the day before it.

THE SPECIAL PUNYA KAALA: In the Sankrantis of the signs of Cancer, Leo, Scorpio, Taurus and Aquarius, the 16 ghatis before Sankranti are specially holy and givers of Punya; in those of the signs of Libra and Aries, it is the 16 ghatis in the middle of the Sankranti that is, the 8 ghatis before and the 8 ghatis after middle of the Sankranti time, which are specially holy and givers of Punya; and in those of the signs of Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces and Capricorn, it is the 16 ghatis after the Sankranti time which are specially holy and givers of Punya.

The Nakshtras called Mridu or Delicate (Mrigashira (1), Rewati (2), Chitra (3) and Anuradha (4)), those called Kshipra (Hasta (5), Ashwini (6), Pushya (7) and Abhijit (8)) Dhanishtha (9), Shravana (10), Kritika (11), Magha (12), Poorvaphalguni (13), Poorvashadha (14), Poorvabhabradabada (15) and Moola (16), these 16 Nakshtras are named as ‘Sama’ Nakshtras. The Nakshtras called Dhruwa (Uttaraphalguni, Uttarashadha, Uttarabhadrapada and Rohini), Vishakha and Punarvasu these 6 Nakshtras are called ‘Brihat’ Nakshtras and Ashlesha, Shatbhisha, Ardra, Swati, Jyeshtha and Bharani, these 6 Nakshtras are referred to as ‘Jaghanya’ Nakshtras.

THE MUHURTAS AND THE EFFECT OF SANKARANTI ACCORDING TO THE DIFFERENT NAMES OF THE NAKSHTRAS: There are 15 Muhurtas in a Sankranti if it happens to occur in the Nakshtras named as 'Jaghanya', 45 Muhurtas if in 'Brihat', and 30 if in 'Sama'. In the month of the Sankranti occurring in the Nakshtras having 15 Muhurtas the rates of grains etc are costly, in that of the Sankranti occurring in the Nakshtras having 45 Muhurtas these are cheap, and in that of the Sankranti occurring in the Nakshtras having 30 Muhurtas these are neither costly nor cheap, these are average.

The same effect prevails in the appearance or rising of the Moon, that is, if the Moon appears or rises in a Jaghanya Nakshtra on the 2nd Tithi of the Shukla Paksha or the bright half of the month, the rates of grains etc are costly in that month, if in a 'Brihat' Nakshtra, these are cheap, and if in a 'Sama' Nakshtra these are average, neither cheap nor costly.

THE VIMSHOPAKA PHALA (EFFECT) OF THE YEAR DUE TO THE SANKRANTI OF CANCER: There are 10 Vimshopakas of the year if there is the Sankranti of the sign of Cancer on Sunday; if on Monday, 20; if on Tuesday, 8; if on Wednesday, 12; if on Thursday, 18; if on Friday, 18; and if on Saturday, 5, that is, in that year, the measure of auspicious effects is equal to the said viswas.

If a Sankranti happens to occur in the ‘Karanas’ of Taitila, Naga and Chatuspada, then at that time the Sun moves in sleeping condition. In the 5 Karanas from the karana of ‘Gara’ (Gara, Vanija, Bhadra, Bava, and Balava) the Sun moves in the sitting condition, and in the karanas of ‘Kinstughana’, Kaulava and Shakuni, the Sun moves in the standing condition. In these conditions in the rates of grains etc. and in the falling of rains there occur the effects which may be regarded respectively as inauspicious, medium and excellent.

If there is the Sankranti of the Sun in the 11 Karanas of 'Bava' etc, then the means of conveyance of the Sankranti respectively are (1) Lion (2) Tiger (3) Pig (4) Donkey (5) Elephant (6) He-Buffalo (7) Horse (8) Dog (9) Ram (10) Ox and (11) Cock. And their clothes are respectively of the following colours: (1) white (2) Yellow (3) Green (4) Pandu (mixed red and white) (5) Red (6) Black (7) Sootish Black (8) Parti-coloured (9) Rug coloured (10) Without clothes (11) Light blackish. Their weapons are respectively (1) Bhushundi (2) Gada or Club (3) Sword (4) Danda or staff (5) Bow (6) Tomar or Gandasa (an instrument to cut grass etc into small pieces) (7) Lance (8) Pasha or an instrument to bind prisoners (9) Ankusha (or rod to drive an elephant) (10) Astra (armour) (11) Arrow. The foods eaten by them are as follows: (1) Grains (2) Kheer (rice and sugar boiled in milk) (3) The grains obtained through begging (4) Fried food named as Pua or Malpua (5) Milk (6) Curd (7) Chitranna or Khichari (boiled rice and pulses) (8) Gur or jaggery (9) Honey (10) Ghrata or boiled butter and (11) Shakkar or raw sugar. The following are respectively their Lepanas (or the things which they rub on their bodies) (1) Kastoori (2) Kumkuma (3) Sandal wood (4) Clay (5) Gorochana (6) Mahavara (7) Marjara-dharma or the Sweat of a Cat (8) Haldi or Turmeric (9) Kaajala or Soot (10) Agru and (11) Kapoor or Camphor. And (1) Devata (god) (2) Bhoot (Ghost or Spirit) (3) Sarpa or Surpent (4) Pakshi or Bird (5) Pashu or Animal (6) Mriga or deer (7) Brahmana (8) Kshtirya (9) Vaishya (10) Shudra (11) Varna Sankara or mixed caste-these are their castes.

THE AUSPICIOUS OR INAUSPICIOUS EFFECTS TO HUMAN BEINGS FROM SANKRANTI ACCORDING TO THE NAKSHTRAS IN WHICH THEY ARE BORN: If the birth Nakshtra falls in the 3 Nakshtras from the Nakshtra which is before the Nakshtras in which a Sankranti occurs, then in that month there will be going out (or travelling); then if it falls in the next 6 Nakshtras, there will be happiness and comfort; then again if it falls in the next 3 Nakshtras, there will be pain; then if it falls in the next 6 Nakshtras there will be the obtainment of clothes, again, if it falls in the next 3 Nakshtras, there will be loss of wealth, and if it falls in the next 6 Nakshtras there will be gains of wealth.

THE THINGS WHICH SHOULD BE DONE WHEN A PLANET IS STRONG: If the Sun is strong the king should be seen; if the moon, there should be the reading and teaching of the shastras or ancient classics (religious books) if Jupiter, marriage; if Venus, there should be travelling; and if Saturn, learning (from the guru) should be taken. If Tara is strong the Moon is auspicious; if the Moon is strong the Sun is auspicious; and if the Sun is strong, all the planets become strong.

There is the Chandramaasa (the Lunar month) from the Pratipada or the first Tithi of the Shukla Paksha or the bright half of the month to the Amavasya (the 30th Tithi of a month). If there is no Sankranti of the Sun in this Chandramaasa then there is the ‘Adhimaasa’ (additional month) and if there are two ‘Sankrantis of the Sun in it, then there is the ‘Kshaya maasa’ (or lost month). In the ‘Kshayamaasa’ the First Maasa (month) and the next maasa should be taken according to the division of the Tithi. Thus, if the birth or the death occurs in the First half of the Tithi, then the birth day of the native and the annual Shraddha of the dead (the anniversary of the dead) are to be celebrated or performed in the previous month; and if the birth or the death occurs in the second half of the Tithi, then his birthday and his annual Shraddha are to be celebrated or performed in the next month.

THE AUSPICIOUS AND THE VEDHA PLACES (HOUSES) FROM THE JANAMA RASHI OR THE BIRTH RASHI: If the Sun in Gochara or in transit is there in the 6th place or house from the Janama Rashi of the native (the sign in which the Moon is there at the time of birth is referred to as the Janama Rashi of the native) then he is auspicious for him, provided that there is no planet in the 12th House, that is, if there is some planet in the 12th House, there is ‘Vedha’ to the Sun and then the Sun posited in the 6th House be- comes inauspicious and harmful for him. In the same way the Sun in transit is auspicious in the 10th House, but if there is some planet in the 4th House, then there is the Vedha of the Sun. The Sun in transit is auspicious in the 3rd and the 11th House but the Vedha places of these Houses which are respectively the 9th and the 5th House should be without any planet. Similarly, Mars, Saturn and Rahu are auspicious respectively in the 6/11/3 Houses provided that there is no planet respectively in the 9/5/12 Houses, that is, these places (9/5/12) are the Vedha Places of these Planets. The Moon is auspicious in 10/3/11/1/6/7 when there is no planet respectively in the 4/9/8/5/12/2 places. Mercury is auspicious in the 2/4/6/8/10/11 Houses from the Janama Rashi of the native when there is no planet respectively in the 5/3/9/1/8/12 Houses. Jupiter gets auspiciousness in the 5/2/9/7/11 places or Houses from the Native's Janama Rashi when there is no planet respectively in the 4/12/10/3/8 places. Venus is auspicious in the 1/2/3/4/5/8/9/12/11 places from the Native's Janama Rashi, if respectively the 8/7/1/10/9/5/11/6/3 Houses are without any planets. There is no mutual Vedha in those planets who have the relation of father and son between them, that is, there is no inauspicious effect in them (The Sun is the father and Saturn is the son, and the Moon is the father and Mercury is the son). Thus, the Sun is auspicious if he is in the 6th House from the Native's Janama Rashi, and in the 12th House from it all the planets due too Vedha give inauspicious effects; but if Saturn is there in the 12th, there will only be auspicious effect, that is, there will be no Vedha. The planet giving inauspicious effect gives auspicious effect if there is the Vipreeta Vedha (Reverse Vedha); that is, if a planet is situated in the places which are his Vedha places and contray to it there is some planet in his above stated auspicious place, then there is Vipreet Vedha. The effect of Vipreet Vedha has been said to be auspicious. For example, if the Sun is there in the 12th House from the Native's Janama Rashi, and at the same time there is some planet in the 6th House, then there will be Vipreet Vedha and its effect will be auspicious. The Moon in the Shukla Paksha or the bright half of the month is auspicious in the 2/9/5 places, if there remains no planet respectively in the 6/8/4 Houses.
