DIFFERENCE OF OPINION WITH REGARD TO VEDHA: The opinion of Narada and the other Acharyas (teachers of Astrology) is that the Vedha of the planets is from the Janama Rashi (Thus, if the Sun is in the 6th House from the Janama Rashi and if there is some planet in the 12th House from it, then the Sun has Vedha from that planet). But the opinion of Acharaya Kashyap is that Vedha is from the sign of that very planet, that is when the Sun is in the 6th House, there is Vedha if there is some planet in the 12th House from the Sun, or when the Sun is in the 12th House, there is Vedha if there is some planet in the 6th House from the Sun.

According to Acharya Kashyap, both these kinds of Vedha are there in the region between the Himalayas and the Vindhya Mountains (that is, in the Northern India). This Vedha is not defective in other places.

THE EFFECTS OF AN ECLIPSE AS PER THE JANAMA NAKSHTRA AND THE JANAMA RASHI: If an eclipse occurs in the Janama (birth) Nakshtra there occurs the death of the native, if it occurs in the Janama Rashi, the native gets bodily pain; in the 2nd, sign loss; in the 3rd, obtainment of Lakshmi or wealth; in the 4th, mental pain; in the 5th, anxiety; in the 6th, happiness; in the 7th, pain to the native's wife; in the 8th, there occurs the death of the native; in the 9th, there is the loss of respect; in the 10th, the native gets happiness; in the 11th, gains and; in the 12th, destruction or loss of wealth. These are the effects of an eclipse. In the eclipse which gives inauspicious effects, the native should recite Mantras, give Cow, gold as alms or in charity, and should do Japa (or the repeated recitation of a mantra) for pacification, or, it is the opinion of the other Acharyas that the eclipse which gives inauspicious effects should not be seen.

SPECIAL EFFECTS DUE TO THE STRENGTH OF THE MOON: If the Moon is hemmed between Malefic planets or if she is in conjunction with a Malefic Planet or if she is in the 7th place from a Malefic Planet then inspite of being auspicious she gets or becomes inauspicious; And if she is in the Navamsha of a Benefic Planet or of her extreme friend and is aspected by Jupiter, then inspite of being inauspicious she gets or becomes auspicious.

THE STRENGTH OF THE MOON AS PER THE DIFFERENCE OF SHUKLA AND KRISHNA PAKSHA: If the Moon is auspicious in the beginning of the Shukla Paksha or the Bright half of the month (in Pratipada etc.) and if she is inauspicious in the beginning of the Krishna Paksha or the Dark half of the month (in the 16th Tithi etc), then both the Pakshas are auspicious. But this strength of the Moon should be considered only at the time of emergency or of trouble, and not at any other time.

THE VARIED GEMS OF THE PLANETS: The native should wear Ruby for the pleasing of the Sun, Pearl for that of the Moon, Coral for that of Mars, emerald for that of Mercury, Topaz for that of Jupiter, diamond for that of Venus, Sapphire for that of Saturn, Gaumeda for that of Rahu, and Cat's eye for that of Ketu. Gold should also be worn for the pleasing of Mercury.

THE WEARING OF GEMS AS PER ANOTHER WAY. AND THE KNOWLEDGE OF TARA: For the pleasing of Rahu and Ketu the native should wear Lajavarta; for that of Venus and the Moon Silver; for that of Jupiter, Pearl; for that of Saturn, iron; for that of the Sun and Mars, Coral. Count from the birth Nakshtras to the present Nakshtra. The number thus obtained is to be divided by 9. The remainder is the Tara. It is repeated three times.
THE NAMES OF TARAS: 1. Janama, 2. Sampata 3. Vipata 4. Kshema 5. Pratyari, 6. Sadhaka 7. Vadha 8. Maitra 9. Atimaitra, are the 9 Taras and their effects are as per their names.

GIVING OF ALMS FOR THE PACIFICATION OF INAUSPICIOUS TARAS: For the pacification of Vadha (Killing to Death) Tara the native should give in alms gold and Molasses, Gur or jeggery in Vipata Tara, Vegetables in the Taras of all the three re- peating Taras and salt in the Pratyari Tara. Vipata, Pratyari and Vadha these 3 are not auspicious in the first turn, and in the 2nd turn the first charana or quarter of Vipata the last charana or quarter of Pratyari and also of Vadha-these are inauspicious. And all are auspicious in the 3rd turn.

The number of the passed Nakshtra (counting from Ashwini) is to be multiplied by 60. To this should be added the passed ghatis of the present Nakshtra. Then it is to be multiplied by 4 and the product should be divided by 45. the quotient is again to be divided by 12. The remainder is the avastha of the Moon in the order of the 12 signs Aries etc. Example: Suppose the passed Nakshtra is Hasta. Its number from Ashwini is 13. If it is multiplied by 60, the product comes to be 780. To 780 should be added the 10 Bhukta or passed ghatis of the present Nakshtras of Chitra, the resultant figure comes to be 790 which is again multiplied by 4 and the product comes to be 3160. It is divided by 45, and the quotient comes to be 70. If it is divided by 12, the remainder comes to be 10. If the native's Rashi or sign is Aries. then the Avastha of the Moon is 10 which is 'jwara' (fever)-see the speculum of the Avasthas of the Moon.

AUSH DHI SNAANA (MEDICINAL BATH) AND DAKSHINA (GIVING REMUNERATION TO THE BRAHMINS) FOR THE REMOVAL OF THE INAUSPICIOUS OR MALEFIC EFFECTS OF THE PLANETS: In order to get relief from the inauspicious or malefic effects of the planets the native should take the bath in water mixed with Laja (roasted paddy), Kootha, Bariyaar Kauni (a creeper), Motha, Sarasaun, Haldi (Turmeric), Deodaaru and Lodhia.
For the pacification of the inauspicious effects arising from the inauspiciousness of the Sun the native should give a cow with a calf, for the pacification of those arising from that of the Moon, conch; for that of Mars red coloured Ox; for that of Mercury, gold; for that of Jupiter yellow clothes; for that of Venus, white clothes; for that of Saturn, black cow, for that of Rahu, Sword; for that of Ketu, he goat.

THE TIMINGS IN WHICH THE PLANETS GIVE THEIR EFFECTS BEFORE MOVING INTO THE NEXT RASHIS: The Sun gives his effects auspicious or inauspicious 5 days before moving into the next Rashi or sign; Mars, 8 days; Mercury, 7 days; and Venus 7 days. The Moon gives her effects 3 ghatis before moving into the next Rashi or sign; Rahu, 3 months; Saturn, 6 months, and Jupiter 2 months.

THE THINGS WHICH SHOULD BE GIVEN AS ALMS IF THE PANCHANGIYA ANGAS (PARTS OR LIMBS OF THE ALMANAC): The King (the native referred to as King) should give gold if it is the 'Yoga' which is inauspicious; conch, if the Moon; grains, if 'Karana'; rice, if 'Tithi'; gems, if 'day'; Cow, if Nakshtra; gold, if 'Nadi'; and 'Sendha' salt, if Tara.

THE PERIOD IN WHICH THE PLANETS GIVE EFFECTS IN A RASHI OR SIGN AND THE EFFECTS OF THE JANAMA NAKSHTRA AS PER THE DIFFERENCE OF DAYS: The Sun and Mars give their respective effects auspicious or inauspicious when they are in the beginning of a Rashi or sign; Venus and Jupiter, when in the middle; Mercury gives his effects in the whole of the Rashi or sign; and the Moon and Saturn when at the end. In every month if the Janama Nakshtra happens to fall on the days of Sunday etc. (in their right order), then the effects are obtained in the following way: travelling, if on Sunday; gains of grains if on Monday; fear from fire if on Tuesday; excellent intellect, if on Wednesday; gains of clothes, if on Thursday; happiness if on Friday and pain if on Saturday.

AUSPICIOUS TIME FOR THE FIRST APPEARANCE OF THE MENSES: The first appearance of women's menses is auspicious in the Shukla Paksha of the 7 months of Magha, Margashirsha, Baisakha, Ashwina, Phalguna, Jyeshtha and Shravana; on the auspicious days (Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday); in an auspicious Ascendant and in the day time.

EXCELLENT, MEDIUM AND LOW NAKSHTRAS FOR THE FIRST APPEARANCE OF WOMEN'S MENSES: The first appearance of women's menses is auspicious if it occurs in the 15 Nakshtras of Shravana, Dhanishtha, Shatabhisha, the Nakshtras named as Mridu or Delicate (Mrigashira, Rewati, Chitra, Anuradha) those named as Kshipra (Hasta, Ashwini and Pushya), those named as Dhruwa (Uttaraphalguni, Uttarabhadrapada, Uttarashadha and Rohini) and Swati and on white (clean) clothes. In the 5 Nakshtras of Moola, Punarvasu, Magha, Vishakha and Kritika, the first appearance of women's menses is medium. And it (the first appearance of women's menses) is low or base in the other remaining 7 Nakshtras (Bharani, Ardra, Ashlesha, Poorvaphalguni Jyeshtha, Poorvashadha and Poorvabhadrapada).

THE TIME WHICH SHOULD BE REJECTED IN THE FIRST APPEARANCE OF WOMEN'S MENSES: The first appearance of women's menses is not auspicious on the Bhadra Tithis (described in the 43rd Shloka of chapter 1); during sleep, on the day of a Sankranti, on the Tithis of Amavasya (the 30th Tithi) and Rikta (4/9/14), in the evening time, on the Tithis of Shashthi, Dwadashi and Ashtami (6/12/8) in the Vaidhriti yoga, in the diseased condition, during the period of the eclipses of the Sun and the Moon and in the Yoga of Vyatipaata. The meaning is that if there is the first appearance of women's menses in these inauspicious times there come obstacles in the happiness arising from the birth of issues. Therefore it is auspicious if its pacification is done.

THE MUHURTA FOR THE BATHING OF WOMEN AFTER MENSES: The woman having menses should be asked to take bath after menses in the Nakshtras of Hasta, Swati, Ashwini, Mrigashira, Anuradha, Dhanishtha, those named as Dhruwa (all the 3 Uttaras and Rohini) and Jyestha, on the auspicious Tithis (2/3/5/7/11/12/13), on the auspicious days (Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday). The woman who takes bath after menses in the Nakshtras of Mrigashira, Rewati, Swati, Hasta, Ashwini and Rohini gets pregnant or conceives soon.

THE TIME WHICH IS TO BE REJECTED IN HAVING SEXUAL INTERCOURSE FOR CONCEPTION: The husband should leave all the three gandantas (the Tithi, the Nakshtra, and the Lagna Gandanta), the Vadha and Janama Tara (that is, 7/10/16/19/25th Nakshtras from the birth or Janama Nakshtra), the Nakshtras of Moola Bharani, Ashwini, Rewati and Magha, the time of the eclipse of the Sun and the Moon, the 'Yogas' of Vyatipata and Vaidhriti, the days of the shraddha of the Father and the Mother (the days of their death), the day time, the first half of the Parigha Yoga, the Nakshtra troubled by Utpaata (portent), the Lagna (Ascendant) of the 8th Rashi or sign from the 'Janama Rashi' or sign of birth, the Lagna of a Malefic Planet (1/5/8/10/11) for doing sexual intercourse with his wife after the period of menses has expired, and she has bathed.

FURTHER THINGS WHICH SHOULD BE KNOWN ABOUT THE MUHURTA OF CONCEPTION: The Karana of Bhadra (described in 1/43), Shashthi (the 6th Tithi), the days of festivals, the Rikta Tithis (4/9/14), the evening time, the days of Tuesday, Sunday and Saturday and the 4 nights from the beginning of the menstrual discharge-these should be left for sexual intercourse which is meant for conception.

Sexual intercourse (for conception) is auspicious in the Nakshtras of Uttaraphalguni, Uttarashadha, Uttarabhadrapada, Mrigashira, Hasta, Anuradha, Rohini, Swati, Shravana, Dhanishtha and Shatbhisha.

A FAVOURABLE LAGNA OR ASCENDANT FOR CONCEPTION: If there are Benefic Planets in the Angles (1/4/7/10) and the Trines (9/5); Malefic Planets in the 3/6/11 Houses, there is the aspect of the male planets (the Sun, Mars and Jupiter) on the Ascendant, the Moon and the Ascendant are in the Navamsha of an odd sign and there are the even nights the 4th etc. (4/6/8/10/12/14/16) after the beginning of the menstrual discharge, the sexual intercourse done for conception is auspicious and giver of a son. It is medium in the Nakshtras of Chitra, Punarvasu, Pushya and Ashwini.

THE MUHURTA FOR SIMANTA SAMSKARA: The performing or doing of the Samskara which is named as Simanta is auspicious on the days of Thursday, Sunday, and Tuesday; in the Nakshtras of Mrigashira, Pushya, Moola, Shravana, Punarvasu and Hasta; on the other Tithis except those of the Rikta Tithis, the Amavasya, the 12th, the 6th and the 8th Tithis, (that is on the 1/2/3/5/7/10/11/13 Tithis); when Masapati or the lord of the Month of conception is endowed with strength (since the month in which the deed of conception is performed to the 9th Month, there is the Masapati or Lord of the Month for every month); in the 6th or 8th month from the conception; when the Benefic Planets are in the Angles and Trines; when the Malefic Planets are in the 3/6/11 Houses and when there is the Ascendant and the Navamsha of a Male sign. Or the Simanta Samskara is excellent in the Nakshtras named as Dhruwa (the 3 Uttaras and Rohini) and Rewati, on auspicious days and when there is the Ascendant and the Navamsha of a male sign.

Due to the Sandhis (joints) of the skull of the head, it is called Simanta. There is the brain in the head with which we think and meditate. SIMANTO–NNAYANA (It is an- other name of the Simanta Samskara) means the elevation or the up- ward rising of the brain or the development of the brain. Therefore, the meaning of the SIMANTO–NNAYANA Samsakara means that Samsakara in which the mind of the mother is concentrated on the development of the brain. ‘Punsavana Samskara’ is the Samskara of the development of, the body, while ‘Simantonnayana Samskara that of the mind. In these two Samskaras is included the bodily and the mental development, everything relating to the foetus in the womb.

It is said that the ‘Simantonnayana Samskara should be per- formed in the 4th or the 6th or the 8th month after conception. It is clear from this is that the best time for the Simantonnayana Samskara is when the cells of the brain of the foetus in the womb are build- ing. It is written in the ‘Shareer Sthaana’ Chapter of Sushruta:

that is, in the 5th month (after conception), it is the soul which be- comes more conscious, in the 6th one, the intellect; in the 7th one, the various organs and limbs become more pronounced; in the 8th one, ‘oja’ remains unstable; the infant born in the 8th month does not remain alive because of the lack of ‘oja’. From this statement, it is clear that, as Sushruta opines, in the 5th month (after conception) the soul of the infant in the womb becomes more conscious than it was before this time. “It becomes more conscious than it was before” means this that in the 4th month the Nervous system begins to take shape or is built. It is because of this that the, time of 'Simantonnayana Samskara' has been chosen to be in the 4th month In the chapter 1/14/1 of 'Ashwalayana Grihya Sutra', there is the say-ing "चतुर्थे मासे सीमन्तोन्नयनम्" that is there should be the comple-tion of the Simantonnayanam Samskara in the 4th month. Sushruta has written: "षष्ठे बुद्धि" that is, in the 6th month there begins the development of the intellect of the infant in the womb. Therefore, it is the 6th month also which has been prescribed for the doing of this samskara.

In the 8th month (after conception) the woman is referred to as Dohrada. 'Dohrada' means one who has 2 Hearts - one heart of the woman's own, and the other of the infant in her womb. In the 8th month after conception, the body, the brain and the heart-all these three are fully prepared. Therefore, if the Simantonnayana Samskara has not been done in the 4th month, it may be done in the 6th month, and if it has not been done in the 6th one also it may be done in the 8th one.

After ‘Garbhadhaana’ or Conception the ‘Punsavana Samskara’ should be performed in the 3rd month on the Tithis, days and in the Nakshtras which have been stated as auspicious for the ‘Simanta Samskara’. And after this in the 8th month, in the Nakshtras of Shravana, Rohini and Pushya, in auspicious Lagans or Ascendants or when there is a benefic planet in auspicious Ascendants, and when the 8th House from the Natal Ascendant is auspicious and is without any Malefic Planet, the worship of Lord Vishnu should be performed (for the protection of conception).

It is auspicious to perform the ‘Jaata Karma’ and the ‘Naama Karana’ samskaras of the newly born infant on the other Tithis except in the Parva or festival (14/8/30/15/ the Sankranti of the Sun) and the Rikta Tithis (4/9/14), on an auspicious day, on the 11th or the 12th day from the birth, in the Nakshtras named as Mridu or Delicate (Mrigashira, Rewati, Chitra and Anuradha), in those named as Dhruwa (the 3 Uttaras and Rohini), in those named as Kshipra (Hasta, Ashwini and Pushya) and in those named as ‘Chara’ or Movable (Swati, Punarvasu, Shravana, Dhanishtha and Shatabhisha, in these 16 Nakshtras.

THE MUHURTA FOR THE BATHING OF THE PRASUTI WOMAN (the woman who has been delivered of an infant): The bathing of the Prasuti woman has been spoken of as excellent in the 10 Nakshtras, of Rewati, those named as Dhruwa (the 3 Uttaras and Rohini) Mrigashira, Hasta, Swati, Ashwini and Anuradha and on the days of Sunday, Tuesday and Thursday. the ‘Sutika Snaana’ or the bathing of the Prasuti woman is not auspicious in the 10 Nakshtras, of Ardra, Punarvasu, Pushya, Shravana, Magha, Bharani, those named’ as Mishra or Mixed (Vishakha and Kritika) Moola and Chitra; on the days of Wednesday and Saturday and on the Tithis of Astami (8th), Shashthi (6th), Dwadashi (12th) and Rikta Tithis (4/9/14). The Sutika Snaana is medium in auspiciousness in the remaining 7 Nakshtras of Ashlesha, Poorvaphalguni Jyestha, Poorvashadha, Dhanishtha, Poorvabhadrapada and on the days of Monday and Friday.

THE EFFECTS OF THE TEETHING OF A CHILD: If the child gets teeth in the 1st month after its birth, that child itself gets destroyed; if in the 2nd Month, it destroys the younger brother; if in the 3rd month, the sister; if in the 4th month, the mother; if in the 5th month, the elder brother; if in the 6th month, it gets extreme happiness; if in the 7th month, it gets happiness and comforts from the father; if in the 8th month, the child gets strong; if in the 9th month, it becomes wealthy; and if in the 10th month, it remains happy in life. If the child is born with teeth it brings destruction to its own self, to the father and the mother or if after the birth it gets the upper teeth in the prohibited period, it brings destruction to the father etc.

14. THE MUHURTA FOR THE CRADLING OF THE CHILD. (Swinging of the infant in the cradle for the first time). The 5 Nakshatras from the Nakshatra of the Sun (the Nakshatra in which the Sun is there) at the time when the child is swung for the first time in the cradle are health-giving for the child. After this the 5 Nakshatras are death-bringing. After this in the 5 Nakshatras the child becomes weak and lean. After this in the 5 Nakshatras, the child gets diseased and lastly in the last 7 Nakshatras it gets happiness.

THE MUHURTA FOR THE DOLAROHAN (Swinging the child in a cradle) AND TAKING THE CHILD OUT OF THE HOUSE: The Dolarohana of the child is auspicious in any of the days, 32, 12, 16, 18 and 10 from the day of his birth, on auspicious days (Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday), in the Nakshtras named as Mridu or Delicate (Mrigashira, Rewati, Chitra and Anuradha), in those named as Laghu (Hasta, Ashwini and Pushya) and those named as Dhruwa (the 3 Uttaras and Rohini) - in these 11 Nakshatras.

It is auspicious to bring the child out of the house for the first time in the 4th Month from the Month of the Birth and on the Tithis and days which have been spoken of as auspicious for travelling. Or going of the child out of house is auspicious on the 12th day from the day of birth.

Notes: The Tithis, days and Nakshtras are to be considered even on the 12th day also from the day of the birth.

THE MUHURTA FOR THE JALA POOJANA OF THE PRASUTI WOMAN: The Prasuti woman should not do 'Jala Poojana (worship of water) in the event of Venus and Jupiter being combust, and in the month of Chaitra, in a Mala Maasa (additional month) and in the month of Pausha although one month might have been completed since the time of delivery (A woman performs Jala Poojana or worship of water one month after delivery). The Prasuti woman should perform the ceremony of Jala Poojana on the days of Wednesday, Monday and Thursday, on other Tithis than those of Rikta (4/9/14) and in the Nakshtras of Shravana, Pushya, Punarvasu, Mrigashira, Hasta, Moola and Anuradha.

THE MUHURTA FOR ANNA PRASHANA (The eating of grains for the first time): The Anna-Prashana of male children is auspicious in the even months 6th etc. (6/8/10/12) and that of the female children is auspicious in the odd months 5th etc (5/7/9/11) in the 16 Nakshtras, in those Nakshtras that are named as Mridu or Delicate (Mrigashira, Rewati, Chitra and Anuradha), in those named as Laghu or small (Hasta, Ashwini and Pushya); those named as Chara or Movable (Swati, Punarvasu, Shravana, Dhanishtha and Shatabhisha) and those named as Sthira or Stable (the 3 Uttaras and Rohini). In the Anna Prashana, the Tithis named as Rikta (4/9/14) and those named as Nanda (1/6/11), the Tithis of Astami (8th), of Amavasya (30th) and the Dwadashi (12th), the days of Saturday, Tuesday and Sunday, the Lagnas or Ascendants of the Navamsha of the 8th sign from the Janama Rashi and Janama Lagna and the Ascendants of Pisces, Aries and Scorpio are to be left out (that is, Anna Prashana samskara should not be done in these Nakshtras, etc.)

THE EFFECTS OF THE PLACES OF THE PLANETS IN ANNA PRASHANA: If Anna Prashana is done when there is the ‘Ksheena Chandra’ or the emaciated Moon in the 9/5/12/1/4/7 Houses from the Natal Ascendant the child becomes a beggar; if there is the Full Moon in these Houses he becomes a doer of Yajnasa; if there is Jupiter he gets long-lived; if Mercury is there he becomes a Gyani (one who has the knowledge of the Absolute); if Mars is there he becomes a patient of the humour of Pitta or Bile (or he becomes bilious), if the Sun is there he becomes a patient of the Kushtha disease (Leucoderma); if Saturn is there he becomes a patient of some windy diseases; and if Venus is there the child, male or female, enjoys various kinds of foods and pleasures.

THE MUHURTA FOR THE SEATING OF THE CHILD ON THE GROUND : Making it (the child) wear 'Kati Sutra' the child should be seated on the ground after worshipping in the 5th Month the Earth and the God Varaha, when Mars is strong, on the other Tithis than those named as Riktas (4/9/14), in a Chara or Movable Lagna or Ascendant, on auspicious days and in the Nakshtras named as Sthira or Dhruwa (the 3 Uttaras and Rohini) and in those of Mrigashira Jyeshtha, Anuradha, and in those named as Laghu or small (Hasta, Ashwini and Pushya).

THE DETERMINATIONN OF THE MEANS OF LIVING OF THE CHILD: Seating the child on the ground put before it many things such as clothes, weapon, book, pen, gold and silver. The child will earn his bread or livelihood by that thing which it takes of its own will or desire.

THE MUHURTA FOR EATING TAAMBOOL OR BETEL LEAF: It is better to make the child eat betel leaf at the age of 2.1/ 2 months or at the time of Anna Prashana, on other days than those of Tuesday and Saturday, in the Nakshtras named as Dhruwa (the 3 Uttaras and Rohini) in those named as Mridu or Delicate (Mrigashira, Rewati, Chitra and Anuradha) in those named as Laghu or small (Hasta Ashwini and Pushya), in those of Shravana, Moola, Punarvasu, Jyeshtha, Swati and Dhanishtha, in these 17 Nakshtras, in the Ascendants of Gemini, Capricorn, Virgo, Aquarius, Taurus and Pisces, in the event of the Benefic Planets being in the Angles and the Trines and of the Malefic Planets being in 3/6/11 Houses.

THE MUHURTA FOR KARNA VEDHA OR MAKING HOLE IN THE EARS FOR WEARNING JEWELS: 'The Karna Vedha Samskara' is excellent if it is done leaving, the two months of Chaitra and Pausha, the sleeping time of Lord Vishnu (From Ashadha Shukla Ekadashi or the 11th Tithi of the bright half of the Month of Ashadha to the Kartika Shukla Ekadashi), the month of the birth, the Tithis named as Rikta (4/9/14), even years (2/4 etc) and the Janama Tara (1/10/11 Nakshtra from the Janama or birth Nakshtra, all these—and in the 6/7/8/ month from birth or on the 12/16 day from the day of birth, on the days of Wednesday, Thursday, Friday and Monday, in the odd (3/5 etc) years, in the Nakshtras of Shravana, Dhanishtha, Punarvasu, those named as Mridu or Delicate (Mrigashira, Rewati and Anuradha and those named as Laghu or small (Hasta, Ashwini and Pushya).

'LAGNA SHUDDHI' OR A FAVOURABLE ASCENDANT IN 'KARNA VEDHA': 'Karna Vedha Samskara' is auspicious when the 8th House from the Natal Ascendant is without any Planet in it, Benefic Planets are in the Angles, Trines and in the 3/11 Houses, when there is an Ascendant of the signs of Venus or Jupiter (2/7/9/12) when the Malefic Planets are in the 3/6/11 Houses from the Natal Ascendant and Jupiter is in the Ascendant.

THE TIME WHICH SHOULD BE REJECTED IN DOING AUSPICIOUS DEEDS: It is not auspicious and excellent to establish the image of a god (or goddess) or to build a tank, to celebrate a marriage, to do 'Agni Adhaana' (to use fire in auspicious deeds), to do entry in a newly built house, to do 'Mundana' or the first cutting of a child's hair, to do coronation and to wear 'Yagyopaveeta or Janeu' (sacred thread worn by the Hindus) - all these things - in the Dakshinayana of the Sun, in the childhood, old age and the Combust condition of Jupiter and Venus and at the time of the rising of Ketu: Some Acharyas opine that till one Paksha (15 days) or half a Paksha (7 days) after the rising of Ketu, the above stated auspicious deeds are not auspicious And according to some other Acharya since the rising of Ketu and as long as it remains visible, auspicious deeds should not be done.

After the rising of Venus in the east there is her childhood for 3 days and after her rising in the West there is her childhood for 10 days. And 15 days before her setting in the East and 5 days before her setting in the West there is her old age.
Jupiter has his childhood for 15 days after his rising in the east and in the west both, and he has his old age for 15 days before his setting in the east and in the west both.

28. DIFFERENCE OF OPINION WITH REGARD TO THE CHILDHOOD AND THE OLD AGE (OF JUPITER AND VENUS): Some Acharyas say that there are 10 days for each of the childhood and of the old age respectively after and before the rising and setting of Jupiter and Venus. And some have said that this time is only of 7 days. And some Acharyas have said that for the Muhurta of some extremely important work the time of these stages is only 3 days.

The Moon remains a child for half day after rising and she remains old for 3 days before setting.

Notes: The aforesaid differences seem to have come into being because of keeping the necessity of the Muhurta in mind. It should be accpeted that different Customs prevail in the different regions of the country with regard to the childhood and old age of Jupiter and Venus. Gargacharya has referred to this fact in the shloka given below:

that is, before and after or on both the sides the childhood and old age of Jupiter and Venus should be regarded as 10 days in the places near the Vindhyachala Mountains, 7 days in Ujjain, 6 days in Bengal, 5 days in Huna region and 3 days in the other provinces.

THE EFFECTS OF THE PLANETS POSITED IN THE ANGLES IN THE LAGNA OR ASCENDNAT AT THE TIME OF MUNDANA: If at the time of Chudakarana there is the emaciated Moon in an Angle from the Lagna or Ascendant, there occurs the death of the child, if Mars is there then the child is attacked with a weapon, if Saturn is there then it becomes lame, and if the Sun is there then it suffers from fever; the Mundana is auspicious if Mercury; Jupiter and Venus are in the Angles and Tara is auspicious (that is, it is the 2/4/6/8/9th Tara).

THE DETERMINATION OF MINDANA ON THE MOTHER'S BEING PREGNANT: If the conception of the mother of the child whose Mundana Samskara is to be done is of more than 5 months duration or time, it is not proper to do Mundana and such Mundana should be prohibited; and if the child is of more than 5 years of age then Mundana is auspicious even in the event of the mother's being pregnant.

EXCEPTION OF MALEFIC TARA IN DOING MUNDANA: If at the time of Mundana the Moon is in a Trine, in her own exaltation sign or in the Varga of her friendly planets or in her own divisional chart, then inspite of the Tara's being malefic (the 1/3/5/7th Tara) the Mundana is auspicious. If the Moon in transit being auspicious is in the sign of a Benefic Planet, then even the Malefic Tara becomes auspicious in such things as Mundana, travelling etc.

THE TIME WHICH IS TO BE REJECTED IN THE MUNDANA OF THE ELDER SON: If the child's mother is having menses or is Prasutika (one who is recently delivered of a child) then the Samskaras like 'Mundana' etc should not be performed; and the 'Mundana' of the eldest son should not be done in the month of Jyesha (roughly falling in May/June) According to some Acharya (Acharya Bharadwaja) the Mundana etc should not be done in the month of Margashirsha (roughly falling in Novemeber/December) also.

THE MUHURTA FOR KSHORA-KARMA (making the barber cut the beard moustache and the hair of the head). It is auspicious to clean the teeth, to get ‘Kshora Karma’ done and to get the nails cut on the tithis, days and the Nakshtras which have been stated as proper and auspicious for the Muhurta of Mundana. But ‘Kshora-Karma’ etc. should be left and should not be done on the days of Saturday, Tuesday and Sunday, on the 9th day from the previous Kshora, in the evening time, on the Tithis named’ as Rikta (4/9/14) on the Tithis of Parva and in the night. One who wants his well be-ing and his benefit should not clean his teeth, should not do Kshora Karma and should not cut his nails without ‘aasana’ (or mat) for sit-ting, during war on the battlefield, in some (other) village, on the day of travelling, after having bath, after oiling and after having taken meal.

SPECIAL TIME FOR KSHORA KARMA: With the permission of a Brahmin or of the king to take part in a yajna, at the time of the death of father and mother and on the occasion of relief of a prisoner from the prison, Kshora-Karma may be done on those days which have been rejected for such Karma. The man whose wife is pregnant should not do the carrying of a dead body to the crema-tion-place, the travelling to a place of pilgrimage or to a foreign coun-try, bathing in the sea and Kshora Karma.

Of the afore-said Nakshatras used for shaving purposes, the king should shave only after five days of his previous shave. If on the fifth day those Nakshtras are not found available then one should shave in the muhurta of shaving Nakshtra, as it is considered auspi-cious. If a person repeatedly does Kshora-Karma within a year, 6 times in the Nakshtras of Kritika, 3 times in that of Anuradha, 8 times in that of Rohini, 4 times in that of Magha and 4 times in that of Uttaraphalguni, he is subjected to death, that is, Kshora Karma should not be done in these Nakshtras.

THE MUHURTA FOR THE BEGINNING OF LEARNING LETTERS BY CHILDREN: In the 5th year from the birth after mak-ing the child worship Lord Ganesha, Lord Vishnu, goddess Saraswati, and goddess Laxmi, it (the child) should be taught the writing of the letters or it should be given the knowledge of the letters of the alphabet on the Tithis of 11,12,10,2,6,5, and 3, in the Nakshtras named as Laghu or small (Hasta, Ashwini and Pushya), in those of Shravana Swati, Rewati, Punarvasu, Ardra, Chitra and Anuradha, in the auspicious or benefic Lagnas or Ascendants (2/3/6/9/12) except the Lagnas or Ascendants of the Chara Rashis (movable signs) and on auspicious days.

THE MUHURTA FOR THE BEGINNING OF GETTING EDUCATION: In the context of the beginning of getting education by children the auspicious Nakshtras are Mrigashira, Ardra, Punarvasu, Hasta, Chitra, Swati, Shravana, Dhanishtha, Shatabhisha, Ashwini, Moola, Poorvaphalguni, Poorvashadha, Poorvabhadrapada, Pushya and Ashlesha, the auspicious days are Sunday, Thursday, Wednesday and Friday and the auspicious Tithis are 6/5/3/11/12/10/2; and the Lord of the Ascendant running at the time of the beginning of Getting Education should be a benefic planet and there should be benefic planets in the Angles and Trines from the Ascendant.

THE TIME OF UPANAYANA SAMSKARA (the ceremony of investiture with the sacred thread or Janeu): The Upanayana Samskara of the Brahmins has been decided to be done in the 8th or the 5th year from the time of conception or of birth, that of the Kshtriyas in the 6th or the 11th year and that of the Vaishyas in the 8th or the 12th year; (This is an ideal time for the Samskara of Upanayana). If this Samskara is done when twice of the prescribed time has passed, then this Samskara has been regarded as of medium level.

Notes: The word Upanayana is a compound word made up of ‘upa’ which means near and ‘Nayana’ which means taking. Thus it means taking near the Guru or the Acharya for getting education or studying the Vedas.

The idea of Upanayana is of great significance. It refers to the fact that one birth of the child took place at the home of its father and mother and another birth will take place at the home of the Guru. After the ‘Upanayana the child will be referred to as ‘Dwija’ or the twice-born, that is a person who is born twice. ‘Upanayana’ is called Vrata-bandhana also.

The main rite in the Upanayana Samskara is the investiture with the Janeu or the sacred thread. Therefore it is called Yagyopaveeta or Vratabandha Samaskara also. The Samskaras of Upanayana and of Vedarambha are very near to each other so near that these can be hardly differentiated. The Vedarambha Samaskara (getting the edu- cation of the Vedas) begins just with the Upanayana Samaskara even today both these Samskaras are performed at the same time in the Gurukulas (Gurukula means the home of the teacher. In the ancient times, the Shishya or the pupil went to the home of the Guru or teacher to get education. He resided there as long as his edcuation was completed) The word Upanayana itself means that the child is now worthy of and dedicated to get the knowledge of the Vedas.

THE MUHURTA FOR THE UPANAYANA SAMSKARA: It is auspicious to perform the Samskara of Upanayana in the Nakshtras named as Kshipra (Hasta, Ashwini and Pushya), those named as Dhruwa (the 3 uttaras and Rohini), that of Ashlesha, those called Chara or movable (Swati, Punarvasu, Shravana, Dhanishtha and Shatabhisha), that of Moola, those named as Mridu or Delicate (Mrigashira, Rewati, Chitra and Anuradha), those of Poorvaphalguni, Poorvashadha, Poorvabhadrapada and Ardra, on the 5 days of Sunday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday and Monday, on the Tithis of 2/3/5/11/12/10 and in the Shukla Paksha or the bright half of the month. The first 3rd part (that is upto the 5th Tithi of the Krishna Paksha) of the Krishna Paksha is also acceptable. The Upanayana samskara is not to be done in the 3rd part of the day or in the afternoon which is called 'Apranha' in Hindi.

41. THE AUSPICIOUS LAGNA OR ASCENDANT FOR THE UPANAYANA MUHURTA: The Lagna or the Ascendant chosen for the doing of Upanayana should be such in which Venus, Jupiter, the Moon and the Ascendant Lord are not in the 6th and the 8th House. And the Malefic Planets are inauspicious in the 1/8/5 Houses.

THE FAVOURABLE LAGNA OR ASCENDANT IN THE UPANAYANA SAMSKARA: In the Lagna or the Ascendant favourable for the Samskara of Upanayana there should not be the Benefic Planets in the 6/8/12 Houses. If the Malefic Planets are situated in the 3/6/11 Houses, they are auspicious. The Full Moon will be excellent if she is in her highest exaltation in the Ascendant or in her own sign otherwise she is not the indicator of auspiciousness if she is in another sign in the Ascendant.

THE LORDS OF THE VARNAS LIKE BRAHMINS ETC AND OF THE VEDAS: Jupiter and Venus are the Lords of the Brahmins, the Sun and Mars of the Kshtriyas; the Moon is the Lord of the Vaishyas; Mercury of the Shudras; and Saturn of the Antyajas (untouchables). Jupiter, Venus, Mars and Mercury are the Lords respectively of the Rigaveda, Yajurveda, Saamaveda and Atharvaveda.

THE REASONS FOR INDICATING THE LORDS OF THE VARNAS AND THE VEDAS: The day and the Lagna or the Ac- cendant of that planet who is the Lord of the Varna and the Veda of the child, and the strength of the planet described in the chapter of 'Gochara Prakaranam' is extremely auspicious in the Upanayana samskara. The storng position of the planets who are the Lords of the Vedas, of the Sun, the Moon and Jupiter is the best for the Samskara of Upanayana or 'Yagyopaveeta'. If at the time of the Upanayana samaskara Jupiter and Venus (Lords of both the Varnas and the Vedas) are in their enemy's sign, in their deep debilitation sign and are defeated in the planetary war, then the concerned child is devoid of the Vedas and the shastras.

If the 'Upanayana Samskara' of the eldest child who is born in the Brahmin Varna is done in the Nakshtra, the month, the Lagna or the Ascendant and on the Tithi of his birth, then the child is endowed with much education and learning. If the child is of the Varna of Kshtriya or of Vaishya and he is born after the first conception, that is, he is born of the 2nd conception and if his 'Upanayana Samskara' is performed in the above-stated conditions, then he also is endowed with much education and learning.

THE EFFECTS OF THE NAVAMSHA OF THE PLANETS THE SUN ETC IN THE LAGNA OR ASCENDANT OF UPANAYANA: If there is the Navamsha of the Sun in the Lagna or Ascendant in which the ‘Upanayana’ is being performed, then that child will be cruel-minded, if of the Moon he will be stupid, if of Mars he will be a sinner, if of Mercury he will be clever, if of Jupiter he will be the doer of all the 6 deeds which are worth doing (the doing of yagya or Yajna, making some one do Yagya, taking of alms, giving of alms, studying and teaching these are called ‘Shatakarma’), if of Venus he will be the doer of yagya or yajna and wealthy, and if of Saturn he will be stupid.

THE EXCEPTION OF THE INAUSPICIOUS JUPITER: If Jupiter is in his sign of exaltation, own sign or friend's sign, no matter he is in any sign, but he must be in his own Navamsha or in his own Vargottama Navamsha or exalted Navamsha (thus the Jupiter in the sign of Gemini should be of the sign of Gemini in the Navamsha also), then he is excellent (or auspicious) in the 4/8/12 Places or Houses from the sign of birth (the Janama Rashi) also.

If Jupiter is in his debilitation sign or in his enemy's sign (10/3/6/2/7) then he is inauspicious even in an auspicious House.

THE TIME WHICH SHOULD BE REJECTED IN THE UPANAYANA SAMSKARA: The Samskara of Upanayana is not to be performed in the Krishna Paksha or the dark half of the month on the Tithis from Shashthi (the 6th) to Amavasya, on the day of Pradosha (described in the 55th Shloka of this very chapter, on the days of Anadhyaya (on the Tithis which are rejected described in the 54th Shloka of this very chapter), on Saturday, in the 'Apranha Kaala' (in the afternoon) on the day on which there is thunder and lightning in the clouds in the morning and on the Galagraha Tithis (the 13/14/15/30/1/4/7/8/9 Tithis).

THE SPECIALITY ABOUT THE NAVAMSHA OF THE MOON: At the time of Upanayana Samskara the Moon may be in any sign, but if she is in the Navamsha of an auspicious sign, then that child remains engaged in getting education, if she is in the Navamsha of a Malefic sign, then he will be penurious, if she remains in her own Navamsha, he will remain very unhappy. But if the Moon is there in the Nakshtras of Shravana and Punarvasu and then she remains in her own Navamsha, then he will become wealthy.

THE EFFECTS OF THE PLANETS THE SUN ETC. WHEN THEY ARE POSITED IN THE ANGLES: If in the Ascendant which is there at the time of doing the ‘Upanayana Samskara’ the Sun is situated in an angle, the child whose Upanayana is done joins royal or government service; if the Moon is in an angle he becomes a trader or a merchant; if Mars, a trader of arms & weapons (or gets job in the army); if Mercury, a teacher; if Jupiter, an excellent scholar or a learned man; if Venus, wealthy; and if Saturn is placed in an Angle he becomes a servant to the Mlechhas or the low born dirty men.

THE EFFECTS OF JUPITER, VENUS AND THE MOON WHEN THEY ARE IN CONJUNCTION WITH OTHER PLANETS: If Jupiter, Venus and the Moon, all these or even one of them is in conjunction with the Sun (at the time of the 'Upanayana Samskara' of a child) the child whose Upanayana is done will be bereft of good qualities; if with Mars, he will be violent; if with Saturn, cruel; and if with a benefic planet (Mercury), he will be an intelligent scholar or a learned man.

THE AUSPICIOUS AND INAUSPICIOUS EFFECTS OF THE NAVAMSHA OF THE MOON: If the Moon is in the Navamsha of Venus and Venus is in a Trine from the Lagna or Ascendant, and Jupiter is posited in the Lagna or Ascendant then the child whose 'Upanayana Samskara' is done (in such combination) will have the knowledge of all the Vedas; and if the Moon be in the Navamsha of Saturn, Jupiter be in the Lagna or Ascendant and Venus should remain in a Trine, then the child will be extremely cruel and uncivilized.

ANADHYAYA (that is, the Tithis which should be rejected): The 10th Tithi of the Shukla Paksha or bright half of the month of Ashadha, the 2nd Tithi of the Shukla Paksha of Jyeshtha, the 11th Tithi of the Shukla Paksha of Pausha, the 12th Tithi of the Shukla Paksha of Magha and the 1/8/14/15/30 Tithis of the Shukla and Krishna both Pakshas of every month and the day of Sankranti, these (Tithis and days) are named as 'Anadhyaya' in the doing of the 'Upanayana Samskara' that is, the 'Upanayana Samskara' should not be done on these.

THE CHARACTERISTICS OF ‘PRADOSHA’: If there occurs the beginning of the 13th Tithi in the 12th Tithi before midnight, of the 7th Tithi in the 6th Tithi before 1½ Prahara in the night, and of the 4th Tithi in the 3rd Tithi before 1 Prahara in the night, then these 3 Tithis are referred to as the Pradosha Tithis. In this way the 12th, the 6th and the 3rd Tithis are named as Pradosha Tithis.

Notes: The meaning of ‘the Pradosha Night’ is ‘the mouth of the Night’. In this way Pradosha occurs on every day as after the setting of the Sun the beginning of the Night, due to its being the mouth of the night, will be named as Pradosha. This Pradosha is ‘Naityika’, that is, it occurs daily and is the daily occurring Pradosha. the Pradosha which has been referred to in the present Shloka is named as Naimittika Pradosha. The studying and teaching of the Vedas and of the Vedangas (parts of the Vedas) have been prohibited in these Pradoshas.

After the ‘Upanayana Samskara’, another samskara which is called ‘Brahmodana’, is performed on the same day in the evening. In the Brahmodana Samskara a special ‘paaka’ or dish is prepared with sacred food grains. this ‘Paaka’ or dish is named as Brahmodana ‘Paaka’. This Smaskara is performed among the Brahmins. The child is caused to eat ‘the sacred Paaka’. If after the ‘Upanyana Samskara’ and before the ‘Brahmodana Paaka’ there occurs any kind of natural disturbance (the thunder of the clouds, storm or tempest), then the Brahmodana Samskara should be performed after doing the pacification rite.

SAMSKARA ACCORDING TO EACH VEDA: The Upanayana Samskara of the Rigavedis is auspicious in the Nakshtras of Mrigashira, Ardra, Ashlesha, Hasta, Chitra, Swati, Moola and all the 3 Poorvas; that of the Yajurvedis in those of Rewati, Hasta, Anuradha, Mrigashira, Punarvasu, Pushya, Rohini and all the 3 Uttaras; that of the Saamavedis in those of Ashwini, Dhanishtha, Pushya, Hasta, all the 3 Uttaras, Ardra, and Shravana; and that of the Atharvavedis in those of Mrigashira, Rewati, those named as Laghu or small (Hasta, Ashwini and Pushya), Anuradha, Dhanishtha and Punarvasu.

THE PACIFICATION RITE FOR THE AUSPICIOUS DEEDS IF THE CHILD'S MOTHER IS HAVING MENSES: If after the completion of the 'Nandi Shraddha' (At the beginning of every auspicious deed there is done a principal part of that karma or deed, Nandi, that is the Shraddha indicating well being), as ill luck would have it, the child's mother has menses, and there is no proper Lagna or Ascendant after this present one, then the Samskaras of Mundana, Upanayana and marriage etc should be performed on the same day according to the customs after doing the pacification rite, otherwise it is not auspicious (that is, the Samskaras of Mundana etc, are not auspicious without doing the pacification rite.)

THE MUHURTA FOR THE KESHANTA KARMA AND SAMAVARTANA SAMSKARA: (Getting the hair cut and the completion of Brahmacharya): In the Muhurta which has been told as auspicious for Mundana (Stated in the 29th Shloka of this very chapter) Samskara, the doing of 'the Keshanta Karma' is auspicious. This Smaskara is performed in the 16th year. And the Muhurta which has been told as auspicious for the Upanayana Samskara is also auspicious for the 'Samavartana Karma' or the completion of Brahmacharya.

THE IMPORTANCE OF ASCENDANT IN MARRIAGE: A wife having good conduct and charming manners is the giver of Dharma, Artha and Kama (religion, wealth and gratification of senses). The nature, conduct and good qualities of a woman become excellent if her marriage is performed in an auspicious Ascendant. It is because of this that a good Ascendant is considered (or chosen) for marriage as son, good conduct and wealth are bestowed by a good Ascendant of marriage.

First of all the reverend astrologer should be worshipped by presenting him gems and clothes (as gifts) and when he is pleased and is in a good mood he should be asked about a favourable Ascendant for the marriage of the concerned girl.

If the Moon is in the 10/11/3/7/5 Houses in the Horary Chart (Ascendant at the time of asking) and Jupiter aspects her fully, then the marriage will be performed soon or if the Ascendant is Taurus, Libra or Cancer and if it (the Ascendant) is occupied or aspected by a benefic Planet, then also marriage will occur soon: This is the effect that is to be predicted.

There is the obtainment of husband for a girl, that is, it should be predicted that the girl will get married if at the time of asking about her marriage the Moon and Venus both being endowed with strength are posited in an odd sign and are also in the Navamsha of an odd sign and both have their aspect on the Lagna or the Ascendant. And if the Moon and Venus being endowed with strength are posited in an even sign and are also in the Navamsha of an odd sign and have their aspect on the Lagna or the Ascendant, then the marriage of the boy will be decided very soon in the future.

If there is the Moon in the 6/8 Houses in the Horary Chart or if there are Malefic Planets in the Lagna or the Ascendant and there is Mars in the 7th House or there is the Moon in the Lagna or the Ascendant and there is Mars in the 7th House from her, then the girl (about whose marriage the astrologer has been asked) will get widowed in the 8 years from the date of her marriage.

THE YOGA OR COMBINATION OF BEING LICENTIOUS AND MRITAVATSA (THE WOMAN WHO GIVES BIRTH TO CHILDREN BUT THE CHILDREN DIE SOON AFTER BIRTH) If there is some Malefic Planet in the 5th House in the Horary Chart and if he being aspected by his enemy planet is situated in a Malefic Sign, then there is the certainty of the girl's becoming promiscuous or Mritavatsa (that is, either she will be a woman of loose character or her children will not survive).

THE YOGA OR COMBINATION OF THE CANCELLATION OF MARRIAGE AS PER THE HORARY CHART: If the question about a girl's marriage is asked in the Krishna Paksha or in the Dark Half of the Month and if at that time the Moon being in an even sign is situated in the 6th or the 8th House and is aspected by a Malefic Planet, then, as per such Horary Chart, there is the Cancellation of marriage, that is, the marriage does not take place even though all the conditions and the date of the marriage have been decided.

THE PACIFICATION RITE FOR REMOVING THE DEFECT OF THE YOGA OR COMBINATION OF WIDOWHOOD. Having made it certain from the Natal Ascendant or the Horary Chart of the girl that there is the presence of the 'Baala Vidhwa Yoga' (the girl's becoming widow soon after her marriage), the girl should be asked to keep Pippala Vrata and Savitri Vrata (these fasts are explained in the notes) and then she should be married to a match having a long span of longevity in his Natal Ascendant; or, first she should be married according to the religious rites of her religion to the image of Lord Vishnu, to a tree of Pippala and to a Pitcher in an auspicious Muhurta (LAGNA OR ASCENDANT) in a lonely place, and then she is to be married to a match having the Yoga or combination of long span of longevity in his Natal Ascendant. In such a condition the girl does not have the defect of re-marriage and if the above stated rites are performed her Yoga or combination of widowhood is cancelled.

The pandits or the astrologers should predict that the girl (about whom they have been asked) will have the kind of issue (girl or boy) with whom some other (married) woman happens to come there of her own accord and without being invited or asked on the occasion of the Horary Chart

THE MUHURTA FOR CHOOSING BRIDE: In the Nakshtras of Uttarashadha, Swati, Shravana, Poorvaphalguni, Poorvashadha, Poorvabhadrapada, Anuradha, Dhanishtha, Kritika or in the Nakshtras of marriage (described in the 55th Shloka of this very Chapter) first the girl (who is to be chosen as bride) should be pleased with the gifts of clothes, jewels, fruits and flowers and then having done this she should be chosen as bride.

THE MUHURTA FOR THE CHOOSING OF THE BRIDEGROOM OR FOR ENGAGEMENT: The Brahmin or the real brother of the bride should choose the bridegroom or should do the engagement on an auspicious day along with the sound of a song and musical instrument and with clothes, Yagyopaveeta or Janeu (sacred thread worn by the pious or religious Hindus) etc in the Nakshtras named as Dhruwa (the 3 Uttaras and Rohini) in those of Kritika, Poorvaphalguni, Poorva Shadha and Poorvabhadrapada.

THE TIME FOR MARRIAGE AND 'GRAHA SHUDDHI' (SUITABILITY OF THE PLANETS). The arranging of marriage is auspicious at the time when Jupiter is 'Shuddha' or suitable six years after the birth of the daughter in even years 8/10 and so on; when the Sun is 'Shuddha' or suitable in the case of the boy in odd years, 9/11 and so on and when the Moon is 'Shuddha' or suitable in the case of both the boy and the girl.

Notes: The position of Jupiter in a benefic House from the 'Janama Rashi' (the sign in which the Moon is there at the time of birth) of the girl is referred to as 'Guru Shuddhi' (or the favourable position of Jupiter); and the position of the Sun in a benefic house from the 'Janama Rashi' of the boy is referred to as 'Ravi Shuddhi' (or the favourable position of the Sun) and the position of the Moon in a benefic house from the 'Janama Rashis' of both the boy and the girl is referred to as 'Chandra Shuddhi'

PROPER TIME FOR MARRIAGE: Celebrating marriage is auspicious when the Sun is in the signs of Gemini, Aquarius, Capricorn, Scorpio, Taurus and Aries. If the Sun is in the sign of Gemini, then in the month of Ashadha it is only from the Pratipada (the first Tithi of the month) to the 10th Tithi in the Shukla Paksha or the Bright Half of the month that the celebrating of marriage is auspicious. If the Sun is in the sign of Scorpio marriage may be celebrated in Kartika also, if he is in the sign of Capricorn, in Pausha also and if he is in the sign of Aries, in Chaitra also.

THE CONSIDERATION OF THE TIME OF MARRIAGE: If the bridegroom and the bride are the first born of their respective parents, then it is not proper to celebrate their marriage in their Janama Maasa, Janama Nakshtra and Janama Tithi (Month, Nakshtra and Tithi respectively of birth). If both are born of the second conception then the celebration of their marriage in the 'Janama Maasa' etc becomes the giver of son (to the newly married couple), such is the saying of the Pandits or the learned astrologers.

CELEBRATING AND NOT CELEBRATING MARRIAGE IN THE MONTH OF 'JYESTHA': The marriage of the eldest daughter and of the eldest son is not to be celebrated in the month of Jyeshtha. If the daughter is the eldest one she may be married in Jyeshtha to a bridegroom who is not the eldest son of his parents or the eldest son may be married in Jyeshtha also to a bride who is not the eldest daughter of her parents. It is the opinion of some Acharya (Bharadwaja) that the celebration of marriage is auspicious in the month of Jyeshtha also leaving that Jyeshtha month in which the Sun is in the Nakshtra of Kritika and joining in wedlock (celebrating the marriage) of the bride and the bridegroom of the First Conception is also not auspicious.

In one's own family the marriage of a daughter should not be cel- ebrated till the expiry of 6 months after the marriage of a son and the Mundana (first hair cutting) of a child is not to be done till the expiry of 6 months after the marriage of a boy or a girl. Two real brothers should not be joined in wedlock with two real sisters. The marriage of two real brothers or sisters should not be celebrated till 6 months and 'Shraddha' of some one in the family is not to be done in an auspicious deed.

The Quarter Vedha of the Nakshtras is used in the same con- text for brevity.
