30. THE GHAATA TITHIS : The Poorna Tithis (5/10/15) for the natives having Taurus, Virgo and Pisces as their Rashis; the Bhadra Tithis (2/7/12) for those having Gemini and Cancer as their Rashis; the Nanda Tithis (1/6/11) for those having Scorpio and Aries as their Rashis; the Rikta Tithis (4/9/14) for those having Capricorn and Libra as their Rashis; and the Jaya Tithis (3/8/13) for those having Sagittarius, Aquarius and Leo as their Rashis - these Tithis are Ghaata (pain-giving) Tithis. These Tithis are inauspicious and should be rejected when going on a journey.

31. THE GHAATA DAYS : Tuesday for the natives having Capricorn as their Rashi; Saturday for those having Taurus, Leo and Virgo as their Rashis; Monday for those having Gemini as their Rashi; Sunday for those having Aries as their Rashi; Wednesday for those having Cancer as their Rashi; Friday for those having Sagittarius, Scorpio and Pisces as their Rashis; and Thursday for those having Libra and Aquarius as their Rashis - (each of these days) - is the Ghaata Day. Journey is inauspicious on a Ghaata day.

32. THE GHAATA NAKSHTRAS : For the natives having Aries and so on as their Rashis the Nakshtras respectively Magha, Hasta, Swati, Anuradha, Moola, Shravana, Shatabhisha, Rewati, Bharani, Rohini, Ardra and Ashlesha these are ‘Ghaata’ Nakshtras and the making of Journey should be avoided in them.

33. THE GHAATA ASCENDANTS : For the natives having Aries and so on as their Rashis the Ascendants respectively 1, 2, 4, 7, 10, 12, 6, 8, 9, 11, 3 and 5 are Ghaata Ascendants. The learned should avoid them when they make a journey.

34. THE CONSIDERATION OF ‘YOGINI’ : Yogini remains in the Eastern direction on the 9th and the Pratipada Tithis (9/1), in the Agneya direction (South East) on the 3/11 Tithis, in the Southern direction on the 5/13 Tithis, in the Nairirtya direction (South West), on the 4/12 Tithis, in the Western direction on the 6/14 Tithis, in the Vayava direction (North West) on the 7/15 Tithis, in the North-ern direction on the 2/10 Tithis, and in the Ishan (East North) direc-tion on the 8th and the Amavasya Tithis. Yogini is not auspicious if she remains in the front or on the left side.

36. PARIGHA DANDA YOGA : Beginning with Kritika 7 Nakshtras are to be established (put) in each of the Four Directions East and so on. In this figure the line joining the Vayavya (North-West) direction and the Agneya direction (South East) is referred to as 'Parigha Danda'. In a journey there should be no violation of the Parigha Danda. The meaning is that in the Nakshtras in the opposite side to that side of which these Nakshtras divided by 'Parigha Danda' are journey should not be made.

37. THE REMOVAL OF THE DOSHA OF 'PARIGHA DANDA' The king (or any person) should make the journey in the Agneya direction (side) in the Nakshtras of the East side, in the Nairirtya direction in those of the South side, in the Vayavya direction in those of the West side and in the Ishan direction in those of the North side. If the work is of urgent necessity, then leaving the consideration of Dika Shoola, if the Ascendant of the Direction in which the journey is to be made is auspicious or favourable, the journey may be made even though the Parigha Danda is violated.

38. THE NAKSHTRAS OF THE JOURNEY IN ALL THE FOUR DIRECTIONS : In the Nakshtras of Anuradha, Hasta, Pushya and Ashwini the journey in all the Four Directions is auspicious.
If a Retrograde Planet is in an Angle, or if there is the Shadavarga of a Retrograde Planet in the Ascendant, then journey in such an Ascendant is prohibited (that is, it is inauspicious) and the day of a Retrograde Planet is also prohibited.

43. REJECTION OF JOURNEY IN THE AQUARIUS ASCENDANT : The learned should reject as inauspicious, at the time of journey, the Aquarius Ascendant and the Navamsha of the Aquarius in any Ascendant because there is loss of money at every step of the king who travels in these Yogas.

44. INAUSPICIOUS AND AUSPICIOUS ASCENDANT : The person who makes a journey in the Pisces Ascendant and when there is the Navamsha of Pisces in any ascendant gets lost on the way (that is, he strays from his way). And if the Lord of the natal Ascendant and the Lord of the Rashi at the time of birth, both of these are benefic planets and they are in the Ascendant then the journey is auspicious or if the Natal Ascendant or the Rashi at the time of birth is in the Ascendant at the time of birth, even then the journey is auspicious.

45. OTHER INAUSPICIOUS ASCENDANTS : If during the time of journey the 8th sign from the Natal Ascendant or the Rashi at the time of birth; or the 6th sign from the natal Ascendant or the Rashi at the time of birth of the enemy king is there in the Ascendant, or the Lords of these signs are there in the Ascendant, then the traveller king is subjected to death.

46. AUSPICIOUS ASCENDANT AND JOURNEY BY A BOAT: If at the time of journey the Ascendant or the Moon is in his Vargottama Navamsha, then the journey is the giver of desired effects. If they are in a watery sign (Cancer, Capricorn, Aquarius and Pisces) or the Navamsha of the Ascendant is of a Watery sign, then journey by boat is auspicious and it serves all ends or completes all deeds.

47. THE ‘DIGDWAR’ ASCENDANT : The journey which is commenced at the time when the Ascendant of the Digdwar (Indicator of the Directions or sides) rises is the giver of wealth and of victory or success, but the journey made in the Ascendant opposite to the Direction or side is the bringer of loss, destruction and fear from the enemy.

48. THE SECOND AUSPICIOUS ASCENDANT: If the Janama Rashi of the person making a journey is occupied by Benefic Planets or the 8th sign from the Natal Ascendant or the Janama Rashi of the enemy is there in the Ascendant at the time of the journey or the Rashi which is named as Veshi (The second sign from that sign in the horoscope of the person making the journey in which the Sun is there is referred to as Veshi sign) is there in the Ascendant at the time of the journey then the journey is the giver of victory or success or making a journey in the Ascendant which has the Raj Yogas described in the Jataka shastras is the giver of victory or success.

49. THE PLANETRY LORDS OF DIRECTIONS : The Sun, Venus, Mars, Rahu, Saturn, the Moon, Mercury and Jupiter, these are respectively the Lords of the 8 directions East and so on.

Notes: The Sun is the Lord of the Eastern direction, Venus of Agneya (South East), Mars of South, Rahu of Nairirtya (South West), Saturn of West, the Moon of Vayavya (North West), Mercury of North and Jupiter of Ishan (East North).

50. THE SIGNIFICANCE OF THE LORDS OF DIRECTIONS : If in the Ascendant at the time of journey the Lord of the Direction (the direction in which the journey is to be made) is in an Angle, it is proper for the king to make the journey. If the Lord of the Direction joins to form Lalatika Yoga (described in the next shloka) then the king should not make an attack on the army of his enemy.

51. LALATIKA YOGA : If there is the Sun in the Ascendant at the time of journey the Yoga named as ‘Lalatika’ occurs in the East; if there be Venus in the 11/12 House from the Ascendant this Yoga occurs in the Agneya direction; if Mars be in the 10th House, it occurs in the Nairirtya direction; if Saturn be in the 7th House, it occurs in the West; if the Moon be in the 5/9 House, it occurs in the Vayavya direction; if Mercury be in the 4th House, it occurs in the North; and if Jupiter be in the 2/3 House, it occurs in the Ishan direction.

Notes: It is quite clear from the shloka that the Lalatika Yoga is formed due to the ‘Dikapati’ or the Lord of the Direction. If in the Ascendant which is there at the time of a journey a Planet is in the same direction of which he is the Lord, then it forms the Lalatika Yoga. Here it becomes clear that if the Lord of a direction is in any other of the 3 Angles than the Angle related to his own direction, the journey is auspicious. Thus if the Sun, (the Lord of the Eastern direction) is in the Ascendant (the House related to the Eastern Direction), then the journey should be rejected. The situation of the Sun in any other of the Angles will be auspicious for a journey.

53. OTHER YOGAS WHICH PROCURE VICTORY : The king who is desrious of getting victory should start in the Hasta Nakshtra, should stay for rest during the Swati and Chitra Nakshtras and then should resume his journey in the Vishakha Nakshtra.

And if the journey is commenced in any of the Nakshtras of Dhanishtha, Rewati and Pushya and it is resumed after staying in his own territory for one night, then such journey procures the gain of lands in the war.

54. THE STRENGTH OF TIME : A journey is auspicious in the morning in all the other directions than in the Eastern, in the Godhuli (the dusk) in all the other ones than in the Western, at mid-night in all the other ones than in the Northern, in the Abhijita Nakshtra in all the other ones than in the Southern.

55. THE NAMES OF THE TWELEVE HOUSE, THE ASCENDANT ETC. : The names of the 12 Houses the Ascendant etc are respectively, Deha (body), Kosha (accumulated wealth), Dhatushka (arms and weapons), Vahana (Conveyance), Mantra (thinking and counselling power), Ari (Enemy), Marga (Way) Ayu (Longevity), Hridaya (Heart), Vyapaar (profession), Agama (gains) and Vyaya (expenditure).

56. AUSPICIOUSNESS AND INAUSPICIOUSNESS IN THE ASCENDANT AT THE TIME OF JOURNEY ACCORDING TO PLANETRY POSITION: In a journey the situation of Benefic Planets in the Angles and Trines from the Ascendant and the situation of Malefic Planets in the 3/11/6/10 Houses from there is auspicious. The Moon in the 1/12/6/8 House from the Ascendant, Saturn in the 10th House, Venus in the 7th House, and the Ascendant Lord in the 7/12/6/8 House - these (combinations) are inauspicious.

57. THE STRENGTH OF COMBINATIONS, NAKSHTRAS ETC. FOR THE KING AND BRAHMINS ETC. : Success has been predicted from the Raj yogas forming in the Ascendant during the journey for the kings or the Kshtriyas, from the strength of the Nakshtras for the Brahmins, for the thieves on the basis of good omens and due to Muhurtas for the other general people.

58. THE YOGA OR COMBINATION LEADING TO VICTORY : If from the Ascendant at the time of journey the Sun be in the 3rd House, the Moon be in the 10th House, Saturn and Mars be in the 6th House, Venus be in the 5th House, Mercury be in the 4th House and Jupiter be in the Ascendant, then the king who makes a journey (in such combination) soon overcomes his enemies and gets victory.
60. If jupiter be in the Ascendant, the Moon be in the 8th House, and the position of the Sun be in the 6th House, even then the king (or the person making a journey) gets victory or success.

91. THE PLACE WHERE FROM JOURNEY SHOULD BE BEGUN : The king should begin his journey from a temple (or from that room in which worship of gods and goddesses is performed), or from the teacher's room or from his own room or from the room of his principal wife (If he has many wives), after eating the grains which have remained after doing ‘Yagya’ or Havana, with the permission of Brahmins and seeing things of good or auspicious omens and singing religious songs which are sung for having good time.

92. THE THINGS WHICH ARE TO BE DONE IF ONE GETS LATE FROM THE PRESCRIBED TIME IN THE JOURNEY: If one gets late due to some unavoidable reasons in starting on the journey, then in the time fixed for starting, Brahmins should roll yogyopaveeta (the sacred thread worn by Pious Hindus); Kshtriyas, Weapons; Vaishhyas, honey; and Shudras, fruit of Amla or coconut or the thing which a person likes, - (these things should be rolled) in the direction in which the journey is to be made and then the journey should be commenced after doing the necessary work.

93. THE DEFINITION OF A JOURNEY : According to the sage named Garga going from one house to another is referred to as journey. The Muni or Sage named Bhrigu defines a journey as going into the premises of another village from one's own village. In the view of Muni Bharadwaja going to that extent to which the arrow shot by one may reach, is called journey and Muni Vashishtha says that going out of the village is a journey.

94. THE MEASURE OF GOING ON A JOURNEY : Some Acharyas regard as going on a journey if one goes 500 Dhanusha or bow (or the distance of 2000 hands or of 1000 yards) some others, if one does 200 Dhanusha or (800 hands or 400 yards) and still some others, if one does only 10 Dhanusha or bow (40 hands or 20 yards) from his place to the destination (the place where one wants to go); but the person going on the journey should make efforts to go in that very direction from his place in which he wants to go.

95. THE TIME DURING WHICH ONE MAY STAY WHILE MAKING A JOURNEY AND PROHIBITION OF COPULATION OR SEXUAL INTERCOURSE : The king who is independent should not stay, in the course of a journey, for 10 days at one place, a feudal Lord (a small king) for seven nights, and an ordinary person for 5 days. And if he has to stay for more days, then he should restart on the journey on an auspicious day. And the king who is desirous of getting victory over his enemies should not indulge in copulation or sexual intercourse for 7 nights before starting on the journey. If this is not possible, he should not indulge in sexual intercourse at least on the day on which he makes the journey.

69. The journey of the king in a Raj Yoga Karaka Ascendant in which Mercury being endowed with strength be gone in the Ascendant, in an Angle there be Jupiter and in any of the 12/3/6/9 Houses there be the Moon in emaciated condition, is the giver of victory.

97. THE THINGS WHICH SHOULD BE SPECIALLY LEFT WHILE MAKING JOURNEY: If someone makes a journey after eating oil, jaggery, salt and cooked meat, he returns as a patient of some disease; and one who makes a journey after insulting a woman (or his wife) and a Brahmin is subjected to death.

98. THE DOSHA OF UNTIMELY RAINING AND ITS CHARACTERISTICS : If there is rain fall in the four months of Pausha, Magha, Phalguna and Chaitra, it is referred to as untimely raining. In this untimely raining as long as there are no marks of footsteps of animals and men on the earth, there occurs no Dosha, that is, it is only when due to rains there is so much mud on the earth that marks of the footsteps of animals and men are made that there occurs the Dosha of untimely raining.

70. The king who makes a journey in an Ascendant having the combination of Planets in which the 9th, 8th and the 7th House, are without any Malefic Planets and Venus being situated in the 4th or 3rd or the 11th House gets the aspect of Jupiter who is gone in an Angle, gets a great wealth.
71. If Mercury being situated in any of the 6/1/10/4 House gets the aspect of Benefic Planets and the 12/1/7 Houses are without any Malefic Planets, even then the king becomes victorious.

72. THE YOGAS PROCURING KINGDOM . If Jupiter be situated in the Ascendant, in the 10th or the 11th House there be the situation of the Malefic Planets, then by making journey in an Ascendant having such combination of Planets, the king has the obtainment of kingdom. Or by making a journey in an Ascendant having a combination in which Mercury and Venus be situated in the 7th House, in the 4th House there be the situation of the Moon there is the obtainment of kingdom for the king, this has been said by all the Munis.

73. AGAIN THE YOGAS GIVING VICTORY : If Venus be in the 6th House, Jupiter in the Ascendant and the Moon in the 8th House, the king gets victory. Or, if Mercury and Venus be in the 4th House and the Moon be in the 7th House or the Moon being between Mercury and Venus be in the 4th House, that is, on one side of the Moon who is gone in the 4th House there be Mercury and on the other side there be Venus, even then the king gets victorious.

74. If in the Ascendant there be Venus, in the 7th House there be Jupiter, in the 6th House Mars, in the 4th House Mercury and in the 3rd House Saturn, the king gets victory.

Or, if on Thursday Mercury and the Sun be there in the 6th House, the Moon in the 3rd House, Mars in the 10th House, Jupiter be situated in the Ascendant, Venus be there in the 4th House and Saturn in the 11th House, then the journey made by the king procures victory for him.

75. If in the 3rd House there be Mars, in the 8th House Mercury, in the 6th House the Sun and in the Ascendant there be Jupiter, then the king gets victory in the journey made in such Yoga. And if Jupiter, Venus and the Sun be there in the Third and the 4th House, Mars and Saturn be in the 6th House, even then the king gets victory.

76. 'YOGA', 'ADHI YOGA' AND 'YOGADHI YOGA' : If any one of the Planets among Mercury, Jupiter and Venus be in an Angle or in a Trine, then there occurs the combination named as 'YOGA'. And if two of these Planets, that is, either Mercury and Jupiter or Mercury and Venus be there in an Angle or in a Trine, then there occurs the combination named as 'Adhiyoga'. And if all these 3 Planets themselves be in an Angle or in a Trine, then there occurs the combination named 'Yogadhi Yoga'. By making the journey in the combination named as 'YOGA' the person undertaking the journey remains well; in that of 'Adhiyoga' he not only remains well but also kills his enemies; and due to the journey made in the 'Yogadhiyoga' combination he remains well and obtains fame and lands.

77. VIJAYADASHMI : The 10th Tithi of the Shukla Paksha of the Month of Ashwina is known by the name of 'Vijayadashmi'. This Vijayadashmi is the giver of success in all matters. If there occurs the Shravana Nakshtra also on the day of 'Vijaya dashmi', then it is the giver of an extremely auspicious effects, and it is the giver of victory and maker of treaty in the journey of the king undertaking it.

78. THE TIME OF JOURNEY ACCORDING TO THE PURITY OF THE CONSCIENCE AND GOOD OMEN : If the Conscience (of the person undertaking the journey) is pure and there is good omen, then having known the strength of the Ascendant, that is, if the Ascendnat is strong, then the journey made in such a time gives success. The purity of conscience is more excellent than the other factors. Therefore, if there is no purity of conscience, journey should not be made.

80. LEAVING THE CONSIDERATION OF DIKASHOOLA ETC. WHEN THE DAY OF STARTING ON A JOUNEY AND THAT OF REACHING THE OTHER VILLAGE IS THE SAME : If the king has to start from one village and to enter the other village on the same day after travelling, then in such a situation the learned (astrologers) Pandits should have no consideration of the Nakshtra shoola, day shoola, of Venus's being in the front side and of Yogini.

81. THE MUHURTA RELATING TO GOING ON A JOURNEY AND ENTERING THE CITY IN WHICH THE KING WANTS TO GO : If the king is in the position of makig journey and entering the city in which he wants to go on the same day, that is, he can reach his destination on the day of starting, then the Pandits (Astrologers) should consider the Muhurta of time of entering and not of starting.

82. THE TRINAVAMI DOSHA IN THE JOURNEY : There should be no going out (going on a journey again after returning) on the 9th Tithi, in the 9th Nakshtra and on the 9th day from the Tithi on which one has returned from a journey and has entered home; And there should be no entering one's home on the 9th Tihi, in the 9th Nakshtra and on the 9th day from the Tithi of going out on a journey.

83. DUTIES BEFORE GOING ON A JOURNEY : Before go-ing on a journey it is proper that the journey is begun after doing 'havana' or 'yagya', worshipping the gods, saluting the Brahmins, worshipping the Planetary Lord of that Direction in which the jour-ney is to be made, giving alms to the Brahmins and properly medi-tating on the Lord of the Direction in which one is going.

Dohaad: The thing to eat which a pregnant woman has a very strong desire is referred to as Dohaad): In Ashwini the pulse of Urd and Barley, in Bharani Mollasses and Rice, in Kritika ‘Urd’, in Rohini the Curd of cow milk, in Mrigashira the Ghee made from Cow milk, in Ardra cow milk, in Punarvasu meat of deer, in Pushya blood of deer, in Ashlesha ‘Kheer’ (rice and raisins, coconut etc. boiled in milk), in Magha the meat of papiha (a kind of bird), in Poorvaphalguni the meat of deer, in Uttaraphalguni the meat of hare or rabit, in Hasta the rice of Saathi in Chitra the rice of Kangani (a kind of rice) in Swati pua, in Vishakha the Chitra Vichitra bird (a kind of bird), in Anuradha excellent fruit, in Jyeshtha the meat of Tortoise, in Moola the meat of Sarika or Maina (a kind of bird) in Poorvashadha the meat of Goha (a particular creature, it is a reptile), in Uttarashadha the meat of Sahi (porcupine), in Abhijita Moong (A pulse), in Shravana Kichhri (rice and pulse boiled together), in Dhanishtha rice and Moong, in Shatabhisha bread or cake of barley, in Poorvabhadrapada fish and rice, in Uttarabhadrapada kichhhri and in Rewati rice and curd - it is these things after eating, or seeing, or touching which one should start on a journey, that is, one should have the consideration whether these are worth eating (eatable) or not according to one’s caste or region and then at the time of starting on journey one should eat that thing which is eatable for him, and should only see or touch that thing which is not eatable.

89. HOW TO GO ON JOURNEY : At the time of journey first of all one should walk 32 steps on the right foot, then one should ride the means of conveyance which is popular in that direction in which the journey is to be made and then should go in the desired direction after giving Mollasses, Ghee, Gold and Copper vessel to a learned Astrologer.

87. THE DOHAAD OF DAY : Journey on Sunday should be begun after eating Rasala (it is made from the mixture of curd, sugar, pepper, ginger and Ilaichi) on Monday after eating kheer, on Tuesday after drinking kanji, on Wednesday after drinking boiled milk, on Thursday after taking curd, on Friday after drinking fresh milk (unboiled) and on Saturday after taking rice mixed with Mollasses.

88. TITHI DOHAAD : Journey is to be made after using (eating or drinking) or seeing or touching Aakpatra (A vegetable also known as Aak and Madaar) on the Pratipada, the water in which grains of rice for cooking have been rinsed and cleaned, on the 2nd, ghee, on the 3rd, imli (the fruit of a tree), on the 4th, Moong, on the 5th, the water in which gold has been cleaned, on the 6th, Pua (made from wheat flour mixed in water and sugar and cooked in oil or ghee) on the 7th, Bijaura lemon (a kind of Lemon) on the 8th, water, on the 9th, urine of cow on the 10th, barley on the 11th, kheer on the 12th, jaggery, on the 13th, blood, on the 14th and Moong on the Pauranmaasi or on the Amavasya Tithi.

99. THE CONSIDERATION OF JOURNEY WHEN THERE OCCURS THE DOSHA OF UNTIMELY RAINING : If there occurs less rain there is less Dosha and if there occurs more rains there is greater Dosha. When there occurs thunder or there begins rainfall the king should get prepared the golden images of the Sun and of the Moon and these should be given to a Brahmin as alms.

If there occurs adverse omens at the time of journey, then journey may be made after giving ghee and gold at one's own will.

Notes: There occurs no Dosha if the rainfall happens to be on the midway.

100-101. AUSPICIOUS OMENS AT THE TIME OF STARTING ON A JOURNEY : If at the time of going on a journey is seen in front Brahmin, horse, elephant, fruit, curd, cow, mustard, lotus, clean clothes, prostitute, musical instrument, peacock, Papiha (a bird), Mongoose, a tied animal (red-coloured ox has been said to be more auspicious), flesh, auspicious words, flower, sugarcane, pitcher filled with water, umbrella, wet clay, virgin or unmarried girl, gem, pugree, clean white ox, wine, woman having her son in her lap, burning fire, spectacles, kajal-surma (soot), washerman with washed clothes, fish, ghee (butter), throne, a dead body over which there is no weeping, flag, honey, hegoat, weapon, gorochana (material for worship), Khanjana (a bird), Palanquin, Sound of Veda (4 Vedas are the holy books of the Hindus), auspicious deed, auspicious song (hymn) and rod with which an elephant is driven - any of these - then it is a good omen and auspicious-effects-giving in a journey. And if some one is seen with an empty pitcher coming from behind, it is also an auspicious omen.

102,103: INAUSPICIOUS OMENS IN A JOURNEY : If at the time of journey one sees in front of him barren woman, skin (of dead animal), husk, bone, snake, salt, cinder (burning), fuel, impotent man, excretion, oil, lunatic, fat, medicine, enemy, a sanyasi (one who has renounced the world and has devoted himself to the worship of God to get salvation) having long hair, grass, a diseased person, naked person (but not an infant), man who has applied 'ubtana' on his body, men with loose hair, depraved (outcaste), one having lopped limbs, man oppressed with hunger, blood, the blood of a woman fallen due to menses, chameleon, the burning of one's own house, battle of cats, sneezing, man wearing saffron-coloured clothes, jaggery, bale (of cotton), mud, widowed woman, man with bent (curved) body, quarrel in the family, falling off of clothes from the body, the fight of a he-buffalo, black grains (Mollasses, urd), cotton, vomitting, sound of ass or donkey, very angry person, pregnant woman, man who has got his hair cut, wet clothes, bad words (abuse or curse), blind deaf, woman in menses—it is inauspicious.

104. OTHER AUSPICIOUS OMENS: Goha (Godha, a creature), Jahaka (a creature which shrinks when it sees some one), pig, snake, rabbit or hare, the seeing of these or the recitation through one's own mouth or through some one's mouth their names or their sound is auspicious; but if these creatures make sound themselves, it is inauspicious. It is reversed if the creatures are monkey and bear, that is the seeing and the hearing of the sound uttered by them is auspicious. But the recitation of their names by one's own self or by some other person is inauspicious. At the time of crossing a river and reaching the other bank, running away with fear, entering the newly constructed house, war and searching for a lost article, the above stated auspicious omens are inauspicious and inauspicious ones are auspicious, that is, the inauspicious omens (described in shloka no. 102 and 103) alone in these matters are excellent or auspicious. But it is the auspicious omens which have been mentioned for the journey made in order to see the king, that should be regarded as auspicious.

105: THE OMENS HAPPENING TO BE ON THE LEFT SIDE AT THE TIME OF JOURNEY: If Cuckoo, chhipakali or lizzard (a reptile), female pigeon, female pig, rala (a bird), pingla or bhairvi (a bird), musk rat, female jackal and the birds having male names are seen on the left side, then these are auspicious.

109. THE MUHURTA FOR ENTERING ONE'S HOME AFTER RETURNING FROM JOURNEY: After returning from journey entering one's home is auspicious in the Nakshatras named as Mridu or delicate (Mrigashira, Rewati, Chitra, Anuradha) and in those named as Dhruwa or fixed (All the 3 Uttaras and Rohini).
If one enters one's home in the Nakshtras named as Kshipra (Hasta, Ashwini and Pushya) and in those named as Chara or Movable (Swati, Punarvasu, Shravana, Dhanishtha, Shatabhisha) one has to make the journey again. If one enters in the Nakshtra of Vishakha, it destroys one’s wife, if in Kritika, one’s home, if in the Nakshtras named as Tikshna or sharp (Moola, Jyeshtha, Ardra, Ashlesha) one’s son, and if in those named as ugra or intense (All the 3 Poorvas, Bharani and Magha), one’s own self.

107. GENERAL OMENS OF THE RIGHT SIDE: If during journey a Mriga (a deer, except Ruru) and a bird come on the right side of the journey-maker, it is auspicious. If deer in odd member are seen going, it is specially auspicious. And the braying of an ass on the left side is also auspicious.

108. THE REMOVAL OF INAUSPICIOUS OMENS: If when an inauspicious omen occurs in a journey for the first time, the journey should be begun again after staying for the duration of 4 breaths (1 breath = 4 seconds). If an inauspicious omen occurs for the second time also, then the journey should be begun again after staying for 16 Breath and it will be auspicious; but if an inauspicious omen occur for the 3rd time also, then the journey should not be made at all.

110. THE RECAPITULATION OF THE DOSHAS DESCRIBED IN THE CHAPTERS RELATING TO MARRIAGE AND TO JOURNEY: The Doshas arising due to Ayana, Nakshtra, Month, Tithi and day, the being of shoola, Mercury and Venus in the front side, the being of the Lord of Direction in the front side, the retro- gression of Venus, Parigha danda, the period of the menses of a wom- an, the time of ' Asauch' or the unholy period after the birth or the death of some one in the family, and the ceremonies like marriage, should be rejected as improper time for making journey.

111. THE THINGS WHICH SHOULD BE SPECIALLY LEFT WHILE MAKING JOURNEY IN THE SOUTHERN DIRECTION: The 'Mritapaksha' because of the relation with Rahu (the 13 Nakshtras which are to be traversed by Rahu described in the 14th shloka), the Rikta, the 12 th and the 6th Tithis, the days of Saturday, Sunday and Tuesday, the Moon on the left side or on the backside the Mahadala Yoga, these are to be left in all journeys and the Nakshtras of Dhanishtha, Shatabhisha, Poorvabhadrapada, Uttarabhadrapada, Rewati, and Abhijita are to be left in the journey in the Southern direction.

112. If the 8th Sign from the natal Ascendant, the 6th Sign from the natal Ascendant or the 'Janama rashi' of the enemy-are there in the Ascendant at the time of making journey, it is inauspicious; or the position of the 8th Lord from one's own Janama rashi or Janama Lagna (natal Ascendant), or the 6th Lord from the Janama Rashi or Janama lagna of the enemy in the Ascendant at the time of Journey should be rejected when making journey. The presence of the Signs of Aquarius and Pisces or of the navamshas of these Signs, or of the signs rising with their backs should be rejected . The signs of the back side (described in the 49th shloka) in the Ascendant are to be avoided, the position of Saturn in the 10th House from the As- cendant, of Venus in the 7th House, of a Retrograde Planet in an Angle, a day related to a retrograde Planet, and the Doshas which have been mentioned in the chapter relating to marriage are also to be rejected as inauspicious when making journey.

1. 1. The Lords of these Vargas are respectively. Garuda (a bird, the conveyance of Lord Vishnu), Marjara (Tom Cat), Singha (Lion), Shwan (Dog), Sarpa (Snake), Mushaka (Mouse), Mriga (Deer) and Mesha (Ram or he goat)

2. The numbers of these Varga are respectively 1/2/3/4/5/6/7 and 8. The directions of these Vargas are respectively East, Agneya (between East-South), South, Nairirtya (between South and West), West, Vayavya (between West and North), North, and Eshanya (between North and East ) The way of knowing the 'Kakinis' of the native and of the Vil-lage or City according to the 2nd method is as follows : the number of the 'Varga' of the first letter of the name of the native is doubled and to this the number of the Varga of the first letter of the Village or City is added. The Sum thus obtained is divided by 8. The re-mainder indicates the number of the native's Kakini. Similarly, the number of the varga of the first letter of the name of the City or Village is doubled, to this is added the number of the Varga of the first letter of the native's name and the sum thus obtained is divided by 8. The remainder will be the number of the Kakini of the City or the Village. Here is an illustration: suppose there is some person named Mr. Darshan Lal Jain. He wants to live and settle in Agra. Now the first letter of the name of Mr. Darshan Lal Jain is in the 'Ja' varga whose number is 5, and the first letter of the name of the City is in the 'Aa' varga the number of which is 1. The varga number of Mr. Darshan Lal Jain will be doubled and to this will be added the varga number of Agra and the sum thus obtained will be divided by 8

5 × 2 + 1 ÷ 8 = 11 ÷ 8. Here the remainder will be 3. This is the Kakini number of Mr. Darshan Lal Jain. In the same way, the varga number of Agra (1) will be doubled and to this will be added the varga number of Mr. Darshan Lal Jain and the sum thus obtained will be divided by 8

1 × 2 + 5 ÷ 8 = 7 ÷ 8. Here the remainder will be 7. This is the 'Kakini' number of Agra. Here we see that the Kakini number of the city is greater than that of the person who wants to settle there. It means that it is the city which will be rich and not the person. Mr. Darshan Lal Jain, because of having fewer Kakini number, will be poor and will remain in debt. Therefore, settling and living in Agra will not be profitable for Mr. Darshan Lal Jain. It will be harmful for him from the economic point of view. In the latter half of the shloka there is the expression 'यस्याधिको सोऽर्थदः'. It means that 'richer' will be that whose 'Kakini is the greater. Commentators have differently interpreted this sentence. Some of them have explained it in this way: that whose Kakini is the greater becomes "indebted". But this view is not accepted by the sages. OR a Brahmin should make the door of his house in the Western direction, a Kshtriya in the Northern direction, a Vaishya in the Eastern direction and a Shudra in the Southern direction.

TO FIND OUT THE GRAHA DHRUWANKA (CONSTANT OF THE HOUSE): There is the Dhruwa (constant) of 1,2,4 and 8 in the directions East etc. If to the sum of the numbers of the Dhruwas (constants) of those directions in which the doors, 1,2,3, or 4 what so ever number of these is to be made in the various directions 1 is added, and there are the 'Gharas' (houses) having names like Dhruwa etc.

10. THE 16 NAMES OF THE GRAHAS (Houses): (1) Dhruwa, (2) Dhanya, (3) Jaya, (4) Nanda, (5) Khara (6) Kant, (7) Manorama, (8) Sumukha (9) Durmukha, (10) Ugra, (11) Ripuda, (12) Vittada, (13) Nasha, (14) Akranda, (15) Vipula, (16) Vijaya, these are respectively the names of the 16 Grahas.

11,12. TO FIND OUT THE 'AYA' VAAR, ETC. OF A HOUSE ACCORDING TO ANOTHER VIEW: The Pinda or the Area of the house is put in 9 places and in each place it should be multiplied respectively by 9/9/6/8/3/8/8/4/8. then the product should be divided respectively by 8/7/9/12/8/27/15/27/12 ; the remainder will be respectively Aya, Vaar, Ansha, Dhana, Rina, Nakshtra, Tithi, Yoga, Ayu. If the Nakshtra of the Graha (house) obtained in this way is the same as is the Nakshtra of the owner of the house, then there occurs the death of the owner of the house.

13,14. THE CONSIDERATION OF 'VRASHA VAASTU' IN THE BEGINNING OF THE CONSTRUCTION OF HOUSE : By counting 3 Nakshtras from that Nakshtra in which the Sun is situated the numbers are put in the head of the image of the size of "Vrasha' (ox). If the construction of the house is begun in these Nakshtras, the house is put on fire; after this 4 Nakshtras ahead are to be imagined in the front legs , if the construction is begun in these Nakshtras, the effect of it is zero, after this 4 Nakshtras ahead in the rear legs, the effect of which is in the form of the stability of the owner in that house; after this 3 Nakshtras in the back are helpful in the obtainment of wealth; after this 4 Nakshtras are to be imagined in the right womb, there is the obtainment of profit in these Nakshtras; then 3 Nakshtras are to be imagined in the tail, if the construction of house is begun is these Nakshtras, there occurs the destruction of the owner of the house; after this 4 Nakshtras are of the left womb, the effect of these is poverty, after this 3 Nakshtras should be imagined in the mouth of the 'Vrasha' (ox), if the construction of house is begun in these Nakshtras, it proves to be pain giving.

19. THE CONSIDERATION OF RAHU MUKHA IN THE BEGINNING OF HOUSE : In laying the foundation stone of the abode of a god (or of gods) or of a temple the Sun's being in 3 signs from the sign of Pisces, of a man in 3 signs from the sign of Leo, and in the beginning of the digging of a tank in 3 signs from the sign of Capricorn there is the mouth of Rahu in the opposite directions respectively from the direction of Ishan Angle (Ishan, Vayavya, Nairitiya and Agneya) and there is the back of Rahu in the opposite direction to it, that is in the Angle of the back side. In laying the foundation stone the direction or side of back is auspicious, that is, if the mouth be in the Ishan Angle, the foundation stone should be put in the Agneya Angle, if it be in the Vayavya Angle, in the Ishan Angle; if it be in the Nairirtya Angle, in the Vayavya Angle. If it be in the Agneya Angle, in the Nairirtya Angle.

17. INSTRUCTION WITH REGARD TO THE DIRECTION OF THE DOOR ON THE BASIS OF TITHI The house facing the Eastern direction or side should not be constructed from the Pauran masi (15th Tithi) to the 8th Tithi of the Krishna Paksha, that facing the Northern direction from the 9th Tithi of the Krishna Paksha to its 14th Tithi, that facing the Western direction from the Amavasya (the 30th Tithi) to the 8th Tithi of the Shukla Paksha, and that facing the Southern direction from the 9th to the 14th Tithi of the Shukla Paksha. The meaning is that the beginning of the construction of house should be done leaving the Tithis which are inauspicious for the direction in which the door of the house is to be made.

18. AUSPICIOUS TITHIS AND VAARS (DAYS) ETC. FOR THE BEGINNING OF THE CONSTRUCTION OF HOUSE : The beginning of the construction of house is regarded as auspicious on the days and Tithis other than the days of Tuesday and Sunday, the Tithis named as Rikta Tithis (4/9/14), those of Amavasya and Pratipada (the 8th Tithi according to symbol), in the other Ascendants than the Lagna or Ascendant called 'Chala' or Movable (1/4/7/10), when the Benefic Planets are in the other House than the 12th and the 8th House and when the Malefic Planets are in the 3/6/11 Houses, in all the Nakshtras except the Panchaka Nakshtras.

According to this shloka, the leaving of the Panchaka Nakshtras is in reference to the establishing of 'Chaukhata' (the base wood of the door) after the beginning of the construction; and these Nakshtras are to be left only when the house is to be made of wood alone, as in the 48th shloka of chapter 2 there is the clear statement with regard to the collection of wood in the Panchakas which has been prohibited. The reference to it is there in the words "त्यजेच्छय्यावितानं गृहगोपनादि च".

20. THE CONSIDERATION WITH REGARD TO THE CONSTRUCTION OF WELL IN SIDE A HOUSE: If the well is constructed in the middle part of the Vastu (the land on which the house is to be constructed) it causes the loss of wealth of the owner; if in the Ishan Angle, the owner is strengthened; if in the East side, it causes increase in the grandeur of the owner; if in the Agneya Angle, loss (death) of his son; if in the Nairirtya Angle, it causes the death of the owner himself; if in the West side, it is auspicious, if in the Vayavya Angle, it causes pain to the enemy; and if in the North side, it is auspicious for the owner of the house.

22. THE LONGEVITY OF THE HOUSE : If in the Ascendant at the time when the construction of the house is begun Jupiter is posited in the Ascendant, the Sun and Mercury in the 7th House, Venus in the 4th House and Saturn in the 3rd House, then the longevity of the house is 100 years. And if there is Venus in the Ascendant, the Sun be in the 3rd House, Mars be in the 6th House, and Jupiter be in the 5th House, then in such combination of planets the longevity of the house will be 200 years.

23. THE OTHER YOGAS WITH REGARD TO LONGEVITY: If in the Ascendant at the time of beginning the construction of the house there be Venus in the Ascendant, Mercury be in the 10th House, the Sun be in the 11th House and Jupiter be in an Angle except the Ascendant House (that is, he be in 4/7/10 House), then the house has the longevity of 100 years
And if Jupiter be in the 4th House, the Moon be in the 10th House, and Mars and Saturn be in the 11th House, then the longevity of the house will be of 80 years

24. THREE YOGAS WHICH ENSURE A HOUSE HAVING THE BLESSING OF LAXMI, THE GODDESS OF WEALTH FOR EVER OR FOR A LONG TIME : If (in the Ascendant at the time of beginning the construction of the house) Venus be exalted in the Ascendant or Jupiter be in the 4th House of the sign of Cancer, or Saturn be in the 11th House in his exaltation sign, then the house the construction of which has been begun in these 3 Yogas (in any of these 3 yogas) has the blessing of Laxmi, the goddess of wealth for ever or for a very long time.
Notes : Jupiter gets exalted position in the 4th House only when the Ascendant is Aries and the Aries Ascendant being a movable Ascendant at the time of beginning the construction of the house

25. MALEFIC PLANETS AT THE TIME OF BEGINNING THE CONSTRUCTION OF HOUSE: If even one Benefic planet (auspicious effects giving planet) being in the Navamsha of the enemy planet is in the 7th or the 4th House (from the Ascendant), and the planetary Lord of the Varna of the owner of the house (the varnas Brahmin etc. have been described in the 43rd shloka of chapter 5) is also weak, then the house the foundation stone of which has been laid in such yoga of planets is taken possession by some other person within a year only

29. THE CONSIDERATION WITH REGARD TO THE MAKING OF DOOR ACCORDING TO ANOTHER ACHARYA: Four Nakshtras from that Nakshtra in which there is the Sun are on the head of the door; if the door of the house is constructed in these Nakshtras, the owner gets Laxmi or wealth. After this 8 Nakshtras are there in the four corners of the house; if the door is constructed in any of these Nakshtras, the owner has to wander out of his house. After this 8 Nakshtras are there in the four branches of the door. If the door is constructed in these Nakshtras which are there in the branches, then the owner always gets comforts in that house. After this 3 Nakshtras are there in the foot of the door. If the construction of the door is begun in these Nakshtras, it causes the death of the owner. And after this 4 Nakshtras are there in the middle of the door. If the construction of the door is begun in these Nakshtras the owner gets comforts.

27. OTHER INAUSPICIOUS AND COMFORTS AND SON-GIVING YOGAS; If Mars be in any of the Nakshtras of Hasta, Pushya, Rewati, Magha, Poorvashadha and Moola and the day be of Tuesday, the house the construction of which is begun in such yoga, gives to the owner affliction from fire and pain to his son.

And if Mercury happens to be in any of the Nakshtras of Rohini, Ashwini, Uttaraphalguni, Chitra and Hasta and the day happens to be of Wednesday, the house the construction of which is begun in such yoga is the giver of house, comforts and son

28. THE YOGA THE CONSTRUCTION BEGUN IN WHICH MAKES THE HOUSE THE ABODE OF GHOSTS, SPIRITS ETC.: If Saturn happens to be in any of the Nakshtras of Poorva bhadrapada, Uttarabhadrapada, Jyeshtha, Anuradha, Swati and Bharani, and the day happens to be of Saturday, then the house the construction of which is begun in such yoga becomes the abode of demons, ghosts and pretas (spirits).

1. THE MUHURTA FOR ENTERING A NEWLY CONSTRUCTED HOUSE; Entering the house after the king's returning from journey and entering the newly constructed house for the first time is auspicious in the months of Jyeshtha, Magha, Phalguna and Baisakha when the Sun is in 'Uttarayana', in the Nakshtras happening to be in the front of the door of the house, in the Nakshtras named as Dhruwa (the 3 Uttaras and Rohini) and those named as Mridu or Delicate (Mrigashira, Rewati, Chitra and Anuradha), and in the Upachaya (3/6/10/11) and the Sthira or Fixed Sign (2/5/8/11) Ascendant from the Janama Rashi and Natal Ascendant of the owner

2. SPECIAL RULES WITH REGARD TO ENTERING AN OLD DILAPIDATED HOUSE: Entering an old, dilapidated, newly constructed house because of the fear of fire etc. is excellent or auspicious in the months stated above and in the month of Kartika, Margashirsha, and Shravana, and in the Nakshtras of Shatabhisha, Pushya, Swati and Dhanishtha also, and no consideration should be made of the combustion of Jupiter and Venus when entering an old, dilapidated house.

3,4. CONSIDERATION WITH REGARD TO THE PACIFICATION OF EVILS AFFECTING THE NEWLY CONSTRUCTED HOUSE BEFORE ENTERING IT: Before entering a newly constructed house there should be done the Worship of the 17 Nakshtras namely, those named as Mridu or Delicate (Mrigashira, Rewati, Chitra and Anuradha) those named as Dhruwa or Fixed (the three Uttaras and Rohini), those named as Kshipra (Hasta. Ashwini and Pushya), those named as 'Chara' or Movable (Swati, Punarvasu Shravana, Dhanishtha and Shatabhisha) and the Nakshtra of Moola, and Bhoota Bali (a religious rite) should be performed. After this in an auspicious Ascendant in which there are Benefic Planets in the 9/5/1/4/7/10/11/2/3 houses and Malefic Planets are in 3/6/11/ houses and the 4th and the 8th house are without any Planet and the Rashi (sign) which is the 8th in the owner's Natal Ascendant and the Janama Rashi should not be in the Ascendant at the time of entering the house, it is auspicious to enter a newly constructed house. Sunday and Tuesday, the Tithis named as Riktas (4/9/14) the Ascendants which are named as 'Chara' or Movable (1/4/7/10), Amavasya, and the month of Chaitra, these should be left for the Muhurta of entering a newly constructed house. The Bhakoota of the owner of the house also should be auspicious. In such auspicious Muhurta the owner should enter the house taking pitcher filled with water and Brahmins ahead of him.

5. THE CONSIDERATION OF THE SUN'S BEING ON THE LEFT SIDE OF THE LAGNA AT THE TIME OF ENTERING THE HOUSE: If the Sun be 5th Houses ahead from the 8th house from the Ascendant which is fixed for entering the house that is, if the Sun is posited in the 8/910/11 or 12 house (from the Ascendant at the time of entering the house), then he (the Sun) is on the left side for the person entering a house facing the Eastern Direction. And the Sun is on the left side for the person entering a house facing the Southern Direction if he (the Sun) is posited in the 5/6/7/8 or 9 House from the Ascendant at the time of entering the house. If the Sun is posited in the 2/3/4/5 or 6 House he is on the left side for the person entering a house facing the Western Direction. The Sun's being on the left side is auspicious at the time of entering a house. For the person entering a house facing the Northern Direction the Sun is on the left side if he is posited in the 11/12/1/2/ or 3 House. Entering a newly constructed house is auspicious if it is done on Poorna Tithis (5/10/15) in a house having its door facing the Eastern Direction, on the Nanda Tithis (1/6/11) in that facing the Southern Direction, on the Bhadra Tithis (2/7/12) in that facing the Western Direction, on the Jaya Tithis (3/8/13) in that facing the Northern Direction. Entering on the Rikta Tithis (4/9/14) should be altogether rejected.

6. THE CONSIDERATION OF 'KUMBHA CHAKRA' (Kumbha= Pitcher. Kumbha Chakra is explained in the shloka) Counting from the Nakshtra in which the Sun is there to the Nakshtra at the time of entering the house, one Nakshtra is supposed to be in the mouth of the imagined shape of a pitcher. If entering is done on that day the house catches fire and is burnt. Then 4 Nakshtras after this are in the East. Due to entering in these Nakshtras the owner is not able to live in that house. Form the Sun's Nakshtra the Nakshtras having numbers from 6 to 9 are in the Southern Direction from the pitcher. If entering is done in these Nakshtras, the house always remains filled with wealth. The Nakshtras from 10 to 13 from the Sun's Nakshtra are in the Western Direction from the pitcher. If the entering is done in these Nakshtras the owner is always getting Laxmi or Wealth. The 4 Nakshtras after these are in the Northern Direction, they cause quarrel and dispute ( if entering is done in them), then 4 Nakshtras in the womb cause the destruction of the owner; then 3 Nakshtras are in the bottom of the pitcher the effect of which is enabling the owner to live in the house for a long time. After this 3 Nakshtras are supposed to be in the throat of the pitcher, these Nakshtras make the living of the owner in the house eternal (that is, till his death)

7. THE THINGS TO BE DONE AFTER ENTERING: In this way the king should enter his house in an auspicious Ascendant along with an umbrella, flowers, Sound of the Mantras from the Vedas etc.' and having entered there should honour the architects, astrologers, those pandits who know the manner of worshipping the Vastu and of Bhoota Bali, and citizens by giving them land, gold, clothes etc. in charity.
